title: Young airman killed in heavy equipment accident at California Space Force base
summary: Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna was killed in a heavy equipment accident at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, prompting a safety investigation.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A 23-year-old airman from North Carolina died Thursday following a heavy equipment accident at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, officials announced Friday.

The airman was identified as Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna, a member of the 30th Civil Engineer Squadron’s Pavements and Equipment Flight, according to the base’s Space Launch Delta 30 Public Affairs office.

The unit maintains critical infrastructure, including roads and airfields, that supports Vandenberg’s launch, test and range operations under the U.S. Space Force, officials said. The base is responsible for launching satellites into polar orbit and conducting intercontinental ballistic missile tests.
AMERICAN FORCES NETWORK EMPLOYEE FOUND WITH FATAL GUNSHOT WOUND AFTER VEHICLE COLLISION NEAR CALIFORNIA BASE
An official military portrait shows Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna in front of the American flag. (Space Launch Delta 30)
Eneluna was operating heavy equipment when it rolled down an embankment, according to the base. No other personnel were injured in the incident.
"It is with profound sadness that we share the loss of Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna, a member of the 30th Civil Engineer Squadron," Vandenberg Space Force Base said in a statement.
"A1C Eneluna served with honor, humility, and an unwavering commitment to his teammates and the mission. His loss is felt across our Vandenberg family."
US SERVICE MEMBER KILLED IN IRAQ AS TROOPS RECOVER UNIDENTIFIED REMAINS IN JORDAN: CENTCOM
Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna smiles on a couch with two dogs. (Cedric Eneluna/Facebook)
The official cause of death has not yet been determined by the Santa Barbara County Coroner’s Office. Units at Vandenberg are supporting a Safety Investigation Board review into the incident.
According to the base, Eneluna was from Fayetteville, North Carolina, and also spent part of his childhood in the Philippines.

He joined the military on March 5, 2024, and arrived at Vandenberg in August for his first duty assignment, where he became part of the unit’s "Dirt Boyz" team, a group of pavement and heavy equipment specialists.
US SERVICE MEMBER KILLED IN IRAQ AS TROOPS RECOVER UNIDENTIFIED REMAINS IN JORDAN: CENTCOM
Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna poses outdoors with two thumbs up during a hike. (Cedric Eneluna/Facebook)
"During his assignment at Vandenberg, he earned the respect and admiration of those around him through his positive attitude, tireless work ethic, and willingness to help others," the base said.

"He made a lasting impression on his teammates through his character, dedication, and genuine care for others," U.S. Space Force Col. James T. Horne III, commander of Space Launch Delta 30 and Vandenberg Space Force Base, said in a statement.

Eneluna’s squadron commander added that the young service member exemplified the qualities of an outstanding Airman.

"He brought out the best in everyone," U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Seth Poulsen, 30th CES commander, said. "He was always ready to work, always willing to help, and always had a positive attitude. He truly represented what it means to be an Airman."

title: Mass shooting rocks crowded downtown Tucson district, leaving 10 wounded
summary: A gunman opened fire in a crowded entertainment district on East Congress Street, wounding nine people before a Tucson police officer shot a fleeing suspect.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
At least 10 people were wounded in a mass shooting in downtown Tucson, Arizona, early Sunday morning after a gunman opened fire in a crowded entertainment district, according to officials.

The suspect, whose identity has not been released, allegedly tried to flee the scene before he was shot by a responding police officer, the Tucson Police Department (TPD) said. He was taken to a local hospital in life-threatening condition.

No deaths were reported, but nine victims suffered gunshot wounds, according to Mayor Regina Romero. Police said the victims sustained gunshot wounds primarily to their extremities, including their arms and legs.
GUNFIRE SHATTERS TORONTO LATIN STREET FESTIVAL, LEAVING AT LEAST 2 DEAD AND MULTIPLE WOUNDED

A forensics photographer from the Tucson Police Department takes photos of the scene where nine people were injured in a shooting in downtown Tucson early Sunday morning, July 19, 2026. (Mamta Popat/Arizona Daily Star)

"Last night, Tucson experienced another serious and senseless act of gun violence," Romero said in a statement Sunday. "A shooter recklessly began shooting in a crowded area striking nine people before being stopped by a Tucson Police Officer."
Police said the shooting unfolded around 2 a.m. in the 100 block of East Congress Street, a downtown area known for its bars, restaurants and nightlife.
Officers patrolling nearby reportedly heard multiple gunshots and immediately responded on foot, where they encountered a man running from the scene.
TOLEDO POLICE NAME SUSPECT KA NYE TAYLOR IN FESTIVAL SHOOTING THAT INJURED 12, HUNT SECOND GUNMAN

Evidence markers lay near items of clothing as part of the Tucson Police Department investigation where nine people were injured in a shooting in downtown Tucson early Sunday morning, July 19, 2026. (Mamta Popat/Arizona Daily Star)
After the suspect allegedly ignored repeated commands from officers, a uniformed officer fired his weapon, striking the fleeing suspect, TPD said.
Police took the suspect into custody and rendered first aid before Tucson Fire Department personnel transported him to a local hospital.
Responding officers also provided emergency medical aid to several victims before firefighters arrived. All the victims were taken to local hospitals for treatment.
MAJOR APPEALS COURT DECLARES NEW JERSEY AR-15 BAN UNCONSTITUTIONAL IN LANDMARK SECOND AMENDMENT RULING
No officers were injured in the incident.

"Thanks to the quick actions and excellent care provided by our firefighters and police officers, all victims were stabilized and taken to the hospital where we are hopeful they will all recover," Romero said.

The Pima County Sheriff’s Department is leading the investigation into the officer-involved shooting. TPD will also be conducting a separate investigation to determine if any policy violations occurred.
Regina Romero speaks on the first day of the Democratic National Convention (DNC) at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois, on Aug. 19, 2024. (MANDEL NGAN/AFP)

The Democratic mayor also condemned the shooting and pointed to what she described as Arizona's weak gun safety laws.

"Easy access to guns and Arizona’s weak gun safety laws have continued to put all of us at risk," Romero said. "From requiring universal background checks to extreme risk laws to funding violence prevention there is more lawmakers can and should do."
Pima County Sheriff’s Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

title: Bulldog's drowning sparks police probe at dog resort marketed as the 'Disneyland for dogs'
summary: Bruce, a 1-year-old English bulldog, allegedly drowned at Camp Canine in Santa Barbara after ending up in a large-dog yard with unfenced pools.
story: Matthew and Elena Kittle filed a lawsuit against The Bay Clubs Company, claiming a staff member at its El Segundo location dropped their 23‑month‑old son, causing a traumatic brain injury. (Rosen Saba, LLP via Storyful)

A California couple says what should have been a routine pickup at a dog daycare marketed as the "Disneyland for dogs" ended in heartbreak after they were told their beloved English bulldog had drowned while in the facility's care.
The heartbreaking incident has prompted a police investigation and an apology from Camp Canine, which acknowledged in a public statement that it "failed in our responsibility to keep their dog safe."
Bruce, a 1-year-old English bulldog owned by Chris and Ashley Merz of Ventura, died Thursday while in the care of the Santa Barbara boarding and daycare facility.
TENNESSEE WOMAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO DROWN ONE OF HER CHILDREN IN BACKYARD POOL

The Santa Barbara Police Department told Fox News Digital that officers responded to the business in the 800 block of East Montecito Street at approximately 4:45 p.m. Thursday following a report of a dog drowning.
During the initial investigation, officers interviewed Bruce's owners as well as employees who were present when the incident occurred.

"The Santa Barbara Police Department is committed to a thorough investigation into this matter," the department said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The case is actively being investigated by our Criminal Investigative Unit and Animal Control Team."
TEXAS DENTIST ACCUSED OF FATAL MISTAKES AFTER 4-YEAR-OLD DIES DURING DENTAL PROCEDURE
Exterior of Camp Canine dog daycare in Santa Barbara, California (GoFundMe)

According to Ashley Merz's mother, Alison Genet, who spoke with local outlet Noozhawk, Bruce is believed to have drowned sometime between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. The family says they were never notified about his death before arriving to pick him up around 3:30 p.m.
Genet told the outlet the family was instead informed of Bruce's death when they arrived at Camp Canine.
Bruce had attended Camp Canine and trained there for about six months, according to Genet.
DOG SAVED FROM ISIS BY ARMY VETERAN 'KIDNAPPED' FROM FAMILY YARD BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES
Bruce the English bulldog remembered by family after Camp Canine tragedy (GoFundMe)

She said English bulldogs are not natural swimmers and that Bruce was typically placed with small or medium-sized dogs because of his size. However, she said he somehow ended up in the large-dog yard, which contains two unfenced pools.
According to Genet, Camp Canine's owners acknowledged Bruce was not supposed to be in that yard but were unable to explain how he ended up there.
A GoFundMe created by Ashley's sister, Savannah, to help cover Bruce's cremation, memorial expenses and legal costs alleges the family's pain was compounded by how the incident was handled.
Bruce the English bulldog remembered by family after Camp Canine tragedy (GoFundMe)
"What was meant to be a normal day at Camp Canine turned into tragedy when their dog drowned while in the facility's care," the fundraiser states.

"The pain was compounded by the way the situation was handled—they were not contacted when the incident occurred, and only learned of their dog's passing later that day when they arrived to pick him up."

The fundraiser also alleges Bruce's body was returned to his owners in "a storage container in the trunk of a vehicle" and says the family later learned he had not been transported to an emergency veterinary hospital before they were notified.
"My sister and brother-in-law are now left grieving the unimaginable loss of a beloved family member, while trying to understand exactly what happened that day," Savannah wrote.

Camp Canine, which says it has served the Santa Barbara area for 40 years and describes itself on its website as the "Disneyland for dogs," publicly apologized Saturday in a statement posted to Instagram.
"There are no words that can fully express the heartbreak we feel following the tragic loss of a beloved dog while in our care earlier this week," General Manager Jayne Sigman wrote.
"A family entrusted us with a cherished member of their family, and they are now living with an unimaginable loss because we failed in our responsibility to keep their dog safe.
Bruce the English bulldog cuddles with owner before tragic daycare drowning. (GoFundMe)
"We are profoundly sorry. Our hearts are with them as they grieve, and we know that no words can lessen the pain they are experiencing."

title: Unsecured metal pipes impale California sedan in terrifying highway crash

story: Gwinnett County police officer Arianna James recounts her experience jumping into action as a 7-year-old boy is flung atop her police cruiser after multi-car crash on ‘America Reports.’
A driver narrowly escaped a terrifying crash Thursday after unsecured metal pipes from a nearby pickup truck pierced through the back of the driver’s sedan on a Southern California highway.
The incident occurred on a highway in Orange County when a white pickup truck carrying the cargo collided with a gray sedan, the California Highway Patrol (CHP) Santa Ana Area Office said Thursday.
"After investigation, it was determined the white pickup truck loaded with metal pipes crashed into the gray sedan," CHP Santa Ana said in a statement.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT TRUCK DRIVER FROM INDIA ARRESTED IN DEADLY CALIFORNIA HIT-AND-RUN AFTER BIDEN RELEASE

Metal pipes protrude from the shattered rear window of a gray sedan following a two-vehicle collision in Orange County, California, on July 16, 2026. (California Highway Patrol (CHP) Santa Ana Area Office )
"After the initial impact, the unsecured metal pipes from the pickup truck were propelled forward, into the sedan, and through the sedan’s rear window."
Photos released by the agency showed the gray sedan with at least six long metal pipes lodged through the shattered rear windshield, narrowly missing the driver’s side of the vehicle.
Officials said the driver thankfully escaped the two-vehicle crash with only minor injuries.
'SLAP ON THE WRIST': ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT TRUCKER'S SENTENCE IGNITES OUTRAGE AFTER CRASH KILLED 3

A white pickup truck and the interior of a damaged sedan are shown after the loose pipes narrowly missed the driver in Orange County, California, on July 16, 2026. (California Highway Patrol (CHP) Santa Ana Area Office )
CHP used the incident as a warning to motorists about the dangers of unsecured cargo, noting that road debris contributes to hundreds of deaths nationwide each year.

"Unsecured cargo causes crashes every year, leading to hundreds of deaths and thousands of injuries nationwide," the agency said. "When a load isn’t properly secured, everyone on the road is at risk."

Unsecured cargo from a nearby pickup truck impales a vehicle along a Southern California freeway in Orange County, California, on July 16, 2026. (California Highway Patrol (CHP) Santa Ana Area Office )
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The agency reminded drivers to properly secure all cargo before hitting the road, using equipment such as ropes, netting, bungee cords or straps. Officials also advised motorists to use sturdy tarps or covers to prevent debris from falling out and to avoid overloading vehicles.

According to data released last year by the AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety, road debris was a contributing factor in roughly 53,000 crashes annually between 2018 and 2023. Those crashes resulted in an average of about 5,500 injuries and 72 deaths each year.

title: Tipster charged with murder after police say anonymous call helped solve 30-year disappearance
summary: Christopher Popps allegedly sent multiple anonymous tips confessing to the 1993 killing of Patrick Orville Dearth before troopers traced them back to him.
story: Fox News' Lauren Green reports on the detention of a person of interest in Jordan concerning the murder of U.S. mom Jamey Carney in Killarney, Ireland. Carney, a native of Westchester, New York, was reportedly beaten and suffocated.
More than 30 years after an Alaska man vanished without a trace, an anonymous confession breathed new life into the cold case and ultimately led investigators to the alleged killer.

Christopher Popps, 54, of Michigan, was arrested after Alaska State Troopers said they traced the confession back to him, accusing him of fatally shooting his former co-worker, Patrick Orville Dearth, in 1993 before dumping his body inside a barrel off a remote highway.
Dearth, 34, disappeared in November 1993 after he was reported missing to the Fairbanks Police Department. For decades, investigators had few answers.
The breakthrough came on Jan. 22, 2025, when Alaska State Troopers received an anonymous tip from someone claiming to have committed a murder in the Fairbanks area in 1993, according to the agency.
WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT
Fairbanks Police Department involved in decades-old missing person investigation. (Fairbanks Police Department Facebook)

The Alaska Bureau of Investigation's Cold Case Investigation Unit took over the case, but investigators couldn't immediately search the area because it was buried under snow and daylight was limited, Alaska State Troopers spokesperson Austin McDaniel told Alaska Public Media.

When investigators returned in May 2025, they found human remains inside a barrel down a steep embankment near Mile 47 of the Steese Highway. The Alaska State Medical Examiner's Office later identified the remains as Dearth and ruled his death a homicide.
KILLER ADMITS TO DECADES-OLD COLD CASE SLAYING AFTER INVESTIGATORS LEAN ON NEW FORENSIC EVIDENCE: OFFICIALS

A Fairbanks Police Department patrol vehicle. Patrick Orville Dearth was reported missing to the department in November 1993 before his case went cold for more than three decades. (Fairbanks Police Department Facebook)
As investigators dug deeper, they identified the anonymous tipster as Popps.
McDaniel told Alaska Public Media that Popps had made multiple anonymous tips to different Alaska law enforcement agencies claiming responsibility for Dearth's death.
Investigators have not said why they believe he began confessing more than three decades after the killing.
FUGITIVE TIED TO DECADES-OLD SLAYING OF PUNK ROCKER ROOMMATE CAUGHT IN TROPICAL HOT SPOT: FEDS
Alaska wilderness near Fairbanks where troopers investigated the cold-case homicide. (Getty Images)
Authorities said Popps and Dearth worked together in Fairbanks and that an altercation at an auto shop ended with Popps allegedly shooting Dearth.
"Based on our investigation, we determined there was an altercation at an auto shop, which led Popps to shoot Dearth," McDaniel told the outlet.
A Fairbanks grand jury indicted Popps on two counts of second-degree murder on June 25, 2026, and a warrant for his arrest was issued the same day, according to court records.
Michigan State Police arrested Popps near Kalamazoo on July 16. He remains jailed in Kalamazoo County awaiting extradition to Alaska.

As of Friday, Popps did not have an attorney listed in Alaska court records, and no future hearings had been scheduled, according to Alaska Public Media.

title: Lindsay Clancy’s husband could testify for her at trial over deaths of their three children
summary: Lindsay Clancy alleges doctors misdiagnosed her bipolar disorder and prescribed antidepressants that worsened her postpartum psychosis before the tragedy.

The husband of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children, is expected to testify on her behalf at her upcoming trial.

Clancy, a 35-year-old former nurse, is slated to go on trial this week in the murder case of her three young children: Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months. Jury selection is scheduled to begin Monday morning in Plymouth Superior Court.

Patrick Clancy is one of the more than 200 people who could be called to testify. Patrick, along with his wife Lindsay, have maintained that the doctors who treated her misdiagnosed and overmedicated her, causing her to hallucinate voices telling her to kill her kids.
The allegations are central to lawsuits claiming that medical professionals failed to diagnose her escalating postpartum psychosis before the deadly tragedy.
MASSACHUSETTS MOTHER ACCUSED OF STRANGLING HER 3 CHILDREN SEEKS INSANITY DEFENSE

Lindsay Clancy, charged with the murder of her three children in Duxbury in 2023, appears in Plymouth Superior Court on Feb. 20, 2026. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger/USA Today Network via Imagn Images)

In an amended complaint filed in Norfolk Superior Court, Lindsay Clancy alleges a network of psychiatric providers misdiagnosed her, failed to properly treat what she says was bipolar disorder with postpartum onset and prescribed a changing regimen of medications that allegedly worsened her condition before the Jan. 24, 2023, deaths of her children.

The complaint accuses the defendants of medical malpractice and negligence, alleging they failed to recognize that Clancy’s reported "intrusive thoughts" were actually auditory hallucinations that made her a danger to herself and her children.

"Lindsay Clancy did everything a mother in her situation could do," the lawsuit says, alleging she sought treatment, went to emergency rooms, contacted crisis services, admitted herself to hospitals and repeatedly reported her worsening symptoms.

The filing offers a medical-failure narrative of the months before the killings, portraying Clancy, a registered nurse who worked in labor and delivery at Massachusetts General Hospital, as a woman unraveling.
Lindsay Clancy with two of their three children in this undated photo (Lindsay Marie Clancy/ Facebook)
KATHIE LEE GIFFORD ADMITS SHE 'WANTED TO DIE' AFTER MISDIAGNOSIS AND MULTIPLE SURGERIES FOR CHRONIC PAIN
According to the complaint, Clancy began showing signs of hypomania soon after giving birth to Callan in May 2022.

By about 12 weeks postpartum, the filing says, Clancy’s condition shifted into severe anxiety, depression, exhaustion and insomnia. She was allegedly sleeping only a few hours a night and struggling with basic daily activities.

The lawsuit says Clancy first sought psychiatric care in September 2022 and was prescribed Zoloft. After the dose was increased, she allegedly went 48 hours without sleep, developed racing thoughts and suffered worsening anxiety.

The lawsuit alleges that these symptoms should have triggered concern for antidepressant-induced activation and possible bipolar disorder. Instead, the suit alleges, Clancy was moved through a series of medications, including Prozac, Ambien, Remeron, Klonopin, Seroquel, Trazodone, Valium and Amitriptyline, without proper coordination among her providers.

The complaint claims the providers failed to obtain a complete psychiatric history, failed to communicate with one another and failed to recognize that antidepressants appeared to be worsening her symptoms.
Lindsay Clancy's three children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 7-month-old Callan, died. (Lindsay Marie Clancy facebook)
MASSACHUSETTS MOM LINDSAY CLANCY'S 911 DISPATCH REVEALS FRANTIC FIRST RESPONDERS
In late November 2022, after taking Remeron, Clancy allegedly became dissociated, disoriented and unsure what was real, according to the filing.
Days later, after starting Seroquel, she allegedly developed suicidal ideation and began hearing a voice telling her she would not be the same and wanted to die.

Her husband, Patrick, allegedly contacted nurse practitioner Rebecca Jollotta's office on Dec. 15 to report that his wife had suffered a "devastating week" and was hearing voices all day, the complaint says.

The filing also alleges Lindsay Clancy told family members she had thoughts of harming the children. At the same time, she allegedly believed people could hear her thoughts and feared she would be locked in a hospital and lose her children.
Lindsay and Patrick Clancy with two of their three children in this undated photo. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/ Facebook)

Clancy went to Massachusetts General Hospital on Dec. 20, then entered a partial hospitalization program at Women & Infants Hospital in Rhode Island, the lawsuit says.
The complaint alleges Dr. Zobeida Diaz concluded Clancy did not have postpartum depression and rejected bipolar disorder despite severe depression and anxiety scores.

Days later, Clancy admitted herself to McLean Hospital on New Year’s Eve. The complaint says she was placed on a locked unit with suicide checks but did not see a doctor until Jan. 3 because of the holiday weekend. She was discharged Jan. 5 after a five-day stay.

Back in outpatient care, the lawsuit says, Clancy continued to deteriorate.

On Jan. 16, she allegedly reported hallucinations saying, "You should harm the children" and "You should kill yourself." Dr. Jennifer Tufts then prescribed Amitriptyline, another antidepressant, according to the complaint.
On Jan. 23, the suit says, Tufts increased the Amitriptyline dose. That night, Clancy allegedly did not sleep.

The next day, the complaint alleges, Clancy was severely depressed and experiencing nonstop suicidal hallucinations. After her husband left to pick up takeout, a commanding voice allegedly told her it was her "last chance" and ordered her to kill the children so she could kill herself.

The lawsuit claims Clancy then entered a dissociative, dream-like state before strangling the children and trying to kill herself by taking medications, cutting her wrists and neck, and jumping from a second-floor window.

title: Democrat lawmaker's 107 mph traffic stop brings bodycam battle front and center again
summary: The sheriff's office involved in a New Hampshire lawmaker's 107 mph traffic stop lacks body cameras and dashboard cameras due to funding shortfalls.
story: Former Acting DHS Secretary Chad Wolf discusses the White House's new guidance allowing I.C.E. agents to resume traffic stops if at least one agent is wearing a body camera following recent fatal shootings on 'America Reports.'

A New Hampshire Democratic lawmaker's 107 mph traffic stop has thrust the debate over police body cameras and dashboard cameras back into the spotlight after Fox News Digital confirmed the sheriff's office involved in the stop has neither.

The lack of body camera and dashboard camera footage has become a focal point in the legal battle involving state Rep. Ellen Read, who is fighting charges stemming from two Rockingham County traffic stops, including one in which a deputy accused her of driving 107 mph. Read argues both stops violated a provision of the New Hampshire Constitution protecting lawmakers while traveling to and from legislative duties.
Without body camera or dashboard camera footage, there is no official recording of the traffic stop that sparked a constitutional fight over legislative immunity.
Maj. Christopher Bashaw of the Rockingham County Sheriff's Office told Fox News Digital the agency does not use body-worn cameras or dashboard cameras because it lacks funding to purchase them.
DEM LAWMAKER SAYS CONSTITUTION BARRED POLICE FROM STOPPING HER AFTER ALLEGED 100 MPH SPEEDING

New Hampshire state Rep. Ellen Read, pictured during a political demonstration in 2015, is seeking to dismiss two speeding cases by arguing the state constitution protected her from arrest while traveling to or from legislative session. (Getty Images)
"We don't have that either," Bashaw said when asked whether deputies use body cameras or dashboard cameras, adding the sheriff's office would like to equip deputies with the technology.

New Hampshire lawmakers established a Body-Worn and Dashboard Camera Fund in 2021 to provide matching grants to local law enforcement agencies for purchasing cameras and covering maintenance, replacement and data storage costs. All local law enforcement agencies are eligible to apply.

State law also requires agencies that choose to deploy body cameras to adopt policies governing when officers must record law enforcement encounters, including traffic stops. The law, however, does not require agencies to purchase or use body cameras.
ICE RESUMES NATIONWIDE TRAFFIC STOPS UNDER NEW POLICY REQUIRING BODY CAMERAS
Read said she supports funding body cameras even though she questions other forms of law enforcement spending. (iStock)
It is unclear whether the Rockingham County Sheriff's Office has applied for funding through the state grant program.

Read told Fox News Digital she has consistently supported legislation governing body-worn cameras, as well as funding to help law enforcement agencies purchase them. She also said she would be willing to work with the Rockingham County Sheriff's Office to help secure funding for body cameras in the next state budget.
Read said she supports funding body cameras even though she questions other forms of law enforcement spending, including military-grade equipment and expensive vehicles.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
She also disputed the sheriff's office's assertion that she recorded part of the traffic stop on her cellphone.

A police officer wears a body-worn camera affixed to a uniform. New Hampshire established a matching grant program in 2021 to help law enforcement agencies purchase body-worn and dashboard cameras. (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)
"They are incorrect, I wish I had," Read said. "The officers conveniently not wearing/using body cams are the reason that I'm investing in a dash cam."
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

According to Read, the sheriff's office misunderstood what happened during the stop. She said she did not record the encounter and that a witness listening during a cellphone call later testified in court.
Read has argued the constitutional provision protects lawmakers from being delayed while traveling to legislative duties – not from prosecution.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

"I admitted to the officer and in court that I was going about 85 miles an hour on the highway," she said, adding that she was willing to accept a speeding ticket but disputed the deputy's allegation that she was traveling 107 mph and driving recklessly.
The New Hampshire State House, the state capitol building of New Hampshire, on Feb. 16, 2023 in Concord. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Lawrence Friedman, a professor at New England Law, said the constitutional provision dates back centuries and was intended to prevent lawmakers from being delayed while performing their legislative duties – not to provide blanket immunity from traffic stops or criminal prosecution.
GOT A TIP?

"I think it's probably not the case that this provision provides some kind of absolute immunity," Friedman told Fox News Digital. "It's unlikely that a court would say, 'No, you're absolutely immune from arrest for a moving violation that everyone else would be subject to arrest for just because you happen to be a legislator.'"
Friedman also said the New Hampshire Supreme Court's refusal to immediately hear Read's constitutional challenge should not be interpreted as a ruling on the merits of her argument.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
"My understanding is that it's not that her appeal is denied," Friedman said. "The Supreme Court said no because they want to see how it plays out at the trial court."
Bashaw said the constitutional provision was intended to prevent law enforcement from interfering with legislative business, not to shield lawmakers from accountability for dangerous driving.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

"The claim that you're immune from all types of arrests... that'd be like saying you could drive at those speeds, commit a vehicular homicide, and that you are not allowed to be held accountable because you're traveling to and from session," Bashaw said.

Read acknowledged the constitutional language could be modernized while preserving its original intent.
"I did not write this constitutional provision... it was written before cars existed," she said.

title: California man admits targeting 3 Subway restaurants for robberies in less than a week, FBI says
summary: Surveillance footage showed Freddie Alexander Lopez robbing three Subway restaurants over a six-day period in late January and early February. He pleaded guilty to a robbery charge.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A California man admitted Friday to carrying out a string of armed robberies and attempted robberies at three Subway restaurants in the Orange County area.

Freddie Alexander Lopez, 24, of Santa Ana, pleaded guilty to a federal robbery charge after admitting he threatened cashiers with weapons at three Subway restaurants and a donut shop, all over about a six-day period.

At each business he targeted, Lopez entered late at night wearing a dark hoodie and a mask, according to the FBI. He would approach the counter, order a bag of chips or another item and wait for the cashier to open the register before brandishing a weapon and demanding money.
Surveillance footage from the businesses, along with cellphone location data placing Lopez near the establishments at the time of the robberies, helped prosecutors link him to the crimes.
Surveillance footage shows Freddie Alexander Lopez robbing a Subway restaurant in Santa Ana, California, Jan. 27, 2026. Lopez pleaded guilty to a federal robbery charge. (FBI)
CALIFORNIA MEN ACCUSED OF $100K BURGLARY ALLEGEDLY TOOK SELFIES WHILE COMMITTING CRIME
Lopez's spree of robberies began Jan. 27, 2026, when he walked into a Subway in Santa Ana at 11:57 p.m., according to court records.
After pulling a knife on the cashier, Lopez was able to get away with $300, according to a criminal complaint.
During the early morning hours of Jan. 30, Lopez entered a Subway in Fountain Valley and once again demanded money while threatening the cashier with a knife, according to his plea agreement.
"Give me all the money, or I'll hurt you," Lopez said, according to witnesses who spoke with law enforcement.
This time, the cashier refused and shut the cash register, prompting Lopez to flee on foot, according to the criminal complaint.
Surveillance footage shows Lopez attempting to rob another Subway restaurant in Fountain Valley, Calif., Jan. 30, 2026, three days after the first robbery. (FBI)
STRING OF BURGLARIES ROCKING LA RESIDENTIAL AREA COMMITTED BY SOUTH AMERICAN GANGS, DA SAYS
Less than 30 minutes later, Lopez robbed a Yum Yum Donuts store about 5½ miles from the Subway he had just targeted, investigators said.
Two days later, on Feb. 1, Lopez walked into a third Subway restaurant in Anaheim, according to the criminal complaint.

Surveillance footage reviewed by the FBI showed Lopez was armed with what appeared to be a black pistol. When the female cashier refused to give him money, the footage showed him jumping over the counter and trying to wrestle the key to the register out of her hand.
After Lopez failed to get the key and could not open the register with the touch screen, he left the restaurant, according to the criminal complaint.
Surveillance footage shows Lopez brandishing what appears to be a pistol while trying to rob a Subway restaurant in Anaheim on Feb. 1, 2026. (FBI)
SOUTH AMERICAN CRIME TOURISM CREW STOLE $24M IN NATIONWIDE LUXURY HEISTS OPERATING FROM BOGUS CAR RENTAL: FEDS
On Feb. 6, the Santa Ana Police Department arrested Lopez during a traffic stop, believing his vehicle was the one that was driven by the suspect in the robberies, according to the FBI.

Officers found what appeared to be "the same handgun, knife, mask and glasses used during the robberies," the FBI said. Investigators noted that they found a replica gun in his car that appeared to match the one used in the Feb. 1 attempted robbery.
Another surveillance camera from the Anaheim restaurant shows Lopez fighting with the cashier over the cash register key. Authorities said Lopez could not get the key and left. (FBI)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
After his arrest, Lopez was released ahead of his trial but was re-arrested on April 30 on the federal robbery charge.
Lopez is scheduled to be sentenced Oct. 2. He faces a maximum of 20 years in prison.

title: Europe's 'green ideology' climate agenda risks crushing its industry, environment minister warns
summary: Czech Environment Minister Igor Červený warns Europe will "crush" its industrial base unless leaders retreat from aggressive climate policies.
story: Igor Červený tells Fox News Digital that Europe must change course as companies move production abroad and voters demand economic results.

UNITED NATIONS — Europe risks destroying its industrial base unless its leaders retreat from aggressive climate policies and respond to voters demanding economic results, Czech Environment Minister Igor Červený warned in an interview with Fox News Digital.

"If we don’t change the course, we will probably crush the industry," Červený said during his first visit to the United Nations, where he addressed the U.N. High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development.
Červený pointed to the pressure facing European manufacturers, particularly the automotive sector, and warned that companies were increasingly moving production abroad.

The debate comes as Europe faces mounting pressure to revive its economy while maintaining ambitious climate targets. The discussion is increasingly relevant for the United States, Europe's largest trading partner, as Washington and Brussels navigate disagreements over energy policy, industrial competitiveness and the pace of the global transition away from fossil fuels.
TRUMP’S REINDUSTRIALIZATION AGENDA FACES ITS BIGGEST HURDLE — AMERICANS

Ambassador Dan Negrea moderates a panel at the U.S. Mission to the United Nations’ "Trade Over Aid" forum in New York, joined by Czech Environment Minister Igor Cerveny and other participants. (Donald Conahan/ U.S. mission to the U.N.)

"If you look at the market at this moment, mostly in European countries, there is a very bad situation," he said. "We see many companies leave our territory and leave for China or another place in the world."
Without those companies, he said, European governments would lose both tax revenue and jobs.
Červený argued that European governments must find a "win-win" approach that protects the environment without undermining industry and employment.
TRUMP'S EPA CHIEF PUSHES BACK ON CLIMATE SKEPTICS BEING LABELED 'SCIENCE DENIERS'
Protesters hold signs, as Fridays for Future demonstrate for a social and climate-friendly Europe, in Berlin, Germany, May 31, 2024.  (Christian Mang/Reuters)

"We have to be very careful about this and be very reasonable and try to find some solution for both sides," he said. "If you look from a higher perspective at European countries, most of them provided only the green ideology. And I think this is a bad way."
Červený said resistance to the current approach was spreading beyond the Czech Republic, citing Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Germany and some Scandinavian countries.

The Czech Republic has been among several European governments pressing Brussels to ease parts of the Green Deal, including by delaying the bloc’s new carbon market for buildings and road transport and seeking changes to emissions-trading rules that Prague argues are raising energy costs and weakening industrial competitiveness.
TRUMP CELEBRATES AFTER UN CLIMATE COMMITTEE MOVES AWAY FROM ITS MOST EXTREME GLOBAL WARMING SCENARIO
Trade union 'Solidarnosc' and Polish farmers protest against the European Green Deal in Warsaw, Poland, May 10, 2024.  (Kuba Stezycki/Reuters)

Červený’s warning stood in contrast to the position presented by European Commissioner for Environment Jessika Roswall during the ministerial segment of the U.N. High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development in New York on July 13. The annual forum, convened under the U.N. Economic and Social Council, brings governments together to review progress toward the organization’s global development goals.

Roswall, speaking on behalf of the European Union and its member states, said the bloc remained committed to the 2030 Agenda, a U.N. framework adopted in 2015 that sets 17 goals covering issues including poverty, health, clean energy, infrastructure and environmental protection to be pursued by 2030. She warned that progress was being undermined by conflict, inequality and the "triple planetary crisis of climate change, pollution and biodiversity loss."
She called for accelerated climate action, greater investment in renewable energy and low-carbon technologies, and support for a broader green transition.
"The challenge is not the lack of ideas, but the lack of speed," she said. "So let’s speed up together."
European Commissioner for Environment, Water Resilience and a Competitive Circular Economy Jessika Roswall. (Florence Lo/Pool/Reuters)
In his exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Červený also praised President Donald Trump for strengthening European politicians who favor a less regulatory approach.

"I’m glad that Mr. Donald Trump is president again, because this changed many things also in European countries," he said, adding that the United States gives smaller countries such as the Czech Republic a stronger partner in debates in Brussels.
Červený said Europe does not need to abandon sustainability, but should pursue it gradually and in cooperation with industry.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
People attend a protest as part of the Global Climate Strike of the movement 'Fridays for Future' in Vienna, Austria, October 10, 2025. (Lisa Leutner/Reuters)
"We have to change the course," he said, "because we don’t want to lose our industry, our economy, our benefits for society and the environment as well."

title: Tate brothers to remain behind bars for now as UK seeks extradition on rape, trafficking charges
summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate will remain behind bars for now after appearing in a Miami federal courtroom as they begin fighting Britain's extradition request on 59 charges, including rape and human trafficking.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate will remain behind bars for now after appearing in federal court in Miami Monday, where they formally began fighting the United Kingdom's bid to extradite the controversial brothers on dozens of charges, including rape and human trafficking.

During the brief hearing, U.S. Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis informed the brothers they were being held on a provisional arrest warrant from the U.K. and that extradition proceedings were already underway.
The judge later scheduled a status hearing for July 27 as the brothers prepare to challenge both the extradition request and whether they should remain in custody while the case moves forward.
Attorney Joseph McBride told reporters that the brothers are innocent and said he does not expect them to be released.
FBI BRINGS ALLEGED CHINA-LINKED HACKER TO US IN RARE EXTRADITION AS PATEL DEFENDS ITALY TRIP

Joseph McBride, lead counsel for Andrew and Tristan Tate, speaks to reporters outside the C. Clyde Atkins United States Courthouse in Miami, Fla., on July 20, 2026. Andrew and Tristan Tate are scheduled to appear before a federal magistrate after they were arrested to face rape and sex trafficking charges in the United Kingdom. McBride said the world knows the brothers are innocent. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
"There will be a series of hearings," McBride said of the extradition process.
Andrew and Tristan Tate appeared wearing gray jail uniforms and shackles and each responded, "Yes, your honor," when Judge Louis advised them of their rights.
The judge also explained that the proceeding was an extradition matter, not a criminal trial, and that the brothers would not be required to attend every hearing.
The brothers were arrested in Miami over the weekend after British authorities announced 38 additional charges involving four additional alleged victims.

Andrew Tate, 39, faces seven additional rape counts, as well as charges related to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child. Tristan Tate, 38, faces charges including two rape counts and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.
British police said the new allegations bring the total number of charges against the brothers to 59. The alleged offenses are said to have occurred between July 2010 and August 2017.

"We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offenses including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child," Malcolm McHaffie, head of the Crown Prosecution Service’s Special Crime Division, said.
DOCTOR INDICTED ON 81 NEW SEXUAL ASSAULT CHARGES IN CASE INVOLVING DOZENS OF VICTIMS
Tristan Tate and Andrew Tate face rape and sex trafficking charges in multiple countries and the United Kingdom is seeking their extradition. (Andrei Pungovschi/Getty Images)
The Tate brothers, who hold dual U.S. and British citizenship, have denied wrongdoing.
They also face separate criminal proceedings in Romania, where authorities have been investigating them since December 2022.

"I want to make it clear there is no place for male violence against women and girls in our society and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us," said assistant chief constable Karena Thomas, lead for Britain's Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire major crime unit.
FORMER PRINCE ANDREW UNDER INVESTIGATION FOR ALLEGED INAPPROPRIATE CONDUCT WITH WOMAN AT ROYAL ASCOT

Andrew Tate speaks to media as he leaves in a vehicle after checking in at a police station as part of his judicial control, which requires him to appear before judicial authorities in Romania when summoned, in Voluntari, Romania, Monday, March 24, 2025. (AP Photo/Vadim Ghirda)
The brothers have built a large online following promoting their views on masculinity and wealth, while Andrew Tate has previously described himself as a misogynist.
Andrew Tate is additionally due to face a civil trial in Britain brought by four women who accuse him of physical and sexual abuse.

The four claimants, who have been granted anonymity, allege Tate subjected them to physical or sexual violence between 2013 and 2015. Two say they were in an intimate relationship with Tate, while two worked for his online webcam business.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Andrew Tate denies those allegations. In his written defense, his lawyers said the claims are false and that all sexual activity was consensual.
Fox News' Andre Tinoco and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Ukraine unleashes more than 400 drones near Moscow in one of war's biggest attacks
summary: More than 400 drones targeted Moscow in one of Ukraine's largest attacks, striking an oil depot and logistics facilities more than 250 miles from the border.
story: Russian officials say two people were wounded and buildings caught fire after one of the largest drone attacks on the Moscow region. (Reuters.)

Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks of the war against Moscow and the surrounding region overnight, striking an oil depot and logistics facilities more than 250 miles from the Ukrainian border, according to Ukrainian and Russian officials.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 400 Ukrainian drones were launched toward the Moscow region between Sunday evening and early Monday, including 85 that were destroyed while approaching the Russian capital. Russia’s Defense Ministry separately claimed that its forces intercepted 381 drones across Russian regions, the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.
The Russian claims could not be independently verified by Fox News Digital.

At least 10 people were wounded in the Moscow region, including three Chinese nationals, according to regional authorities cited by Reuters. Seven of the injuries were reported in Domodedovo, Russia, where officials said a residential building was struck and a fire broke out at an industrial park near one of Moscow’s main airports.
The scale and reach of the operation suggest Ukraine is moving beyond occasional symbolic attacks on Moscow and building a sustained campaign against the infrastructure that supports Russia’s war.
UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

By simultaneously targeting oil facilities, transportation networks and logistics hubs hundreds of miles from the front, Kyiv is seeking to disrupt the flow of fuel and supplies to Russian forces, reduce revenue available to the Kremlin and force Moscow to divert air-defense systems away from the battlefield.
Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries had doubled since the beginning of 2026, Reuters reported, contributing to refinery shutdowns and reduced production of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
Smoke and flames rise from an industrial facility in Podolsk, Russia, in the Moscow region, after a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack overnight July 20, 2026. (East2west news)
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian forces targeted logistics facilities and an oil depot in the Moscow region.

"Our long-range sanctions have produced results against logistics facilities and an oil depot," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that the targets were more than 400 kilometers (roughly 250 miles) from Ukraine’s border. "We are responding, justly, to every Russian strike against our cities and communities."

Wildberries, a company known as "Russia’s Amazon," said its logistics center in the Podolsk district of Russia was temporarily evacuated as a precaution before resuming normal operations, East2West News reported. Ukraine has accused the company of selling supplies used by the Russian military.
RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Smoke rises from the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Golden Leo after it was struck near Odesa on July 20, 2026. Ukrainian officials said 10 people were killed in the Russian missile attack. (East2west news)

Ksenia Svetlova, associate fellow at Chatham House policy institute based in London, argued that the disruption caused by strikes on fuel infrastructure and companies such as Wildberries is unlikely, by itself, to change President Vladimir Putin’s approach to the war.

"The hardship of the Russian citizen who suffers because of fuel shortages, the strike on a Wildberries warehouse, or forced recruitment does not interest him," Svetlova said. "The war machine is operating at full force, and he has neither the desire nor the ability to stop it."

Svetlova said Putin remains reluctant to announce another mass mobilization after large numbers of young Russians fled the country during the Kremlin’s previous call-up. At the same time, she said, Russia’s military still needs additional troops after recruiting heavily from its prison population and is increasingly pressuring ordinary civilians accused of relatively minor offenses to sign military contracts.

The sweeping Ukrainian operation followed one of Russia’s largest ballistic missile attacks of the war against Kyiv. Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 41 missiles of various types in the overnight barrage, which killed at least one person and wounded 16, Reuters reported Sunday.
The Russian attack also spread into the Black Sea, where a Russian missile attack on the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Golden Leo killed 10 people near Odesa, Reuters reported Monday.
'A NEW KIND OF WAR': INSIDE UKRAINE'S HIDDEN FACTORIES MASS-PRODUCING COMBAT DRONES
An explosion strikes a building in Domodedovo, in the Moscow region, during a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack overnight on July 20, 2026. (East2West news)

Ukrainian officials said the vessel, which was carrying corn, was struck by three cruise missiles and caught fire. Nine crew members and a Ukrainian maritime pilot were killed, while eight other crew members were rescued. The ship’s crew included Indian and Syrian nationals, according to Reuters.

The escalation comes as Zelenskyy faces growing domestic pressure over his removal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a 35-year-old reformer credited with expanding Ukraine’s drone capabilities and seeking to modernize military procurement and management. Fedorov’s supporters viewed him as a rare official willing to challenge entrenched practices, improve oversight of defense spending and push a technology-centered approach to the war.

Thousands of demonstrators gathered following Fedorov’s dismissal, demanding his reinstatement and the removal of commander-in-chief Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi. Protesters have accused Syrskyi of resisting modernization and retaining a rigid command structure that they say contributes to high troop losses. Syrskyi has defended his wartime record and called for unity.

Fedorov publicly accused Syrskyi of blocking his initiatives and sabotaging his work. Zelenskyy said their relationship had deteriorated so badly that the two could no longer work together, but provided little additional explanation for removing Fedorov.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
People protest against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's decision to replace Mykhailo Fedorov as defense minister in Kyiv, Ukraine, July 18, 2026. (Thomas Peter/Reuters)

Zelenskyy indicated Monday that consultations over Ukraine’s military leadership were continuing, saying he had spoken with Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi about ensuring that the experience of every branch of Ukraine’s defense forces was applied in a coordinated manner. He did not announce any decision on Syrskyi’s future.
Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Andy Burnham takes over as UK prime minister, calls for 'new political model'
summary: Andy Burnham enters Downing Street vowing to shift power away from London, but his past criticism of Trump could create early friction with Washington.
story: New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledges major socialist changes, including nationalizing utilities, expanding government housing and re-industrializing Britain.

New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham assumed power Monday morning, vowing to move authority away from London as his new government confronts economic strain, political instability and potential friction with Washington.

"We will change politics, to make it more collaborative, more about problem-solving than point scoring," Burnham said outside 10 Downing Street. "And we will take power out of here and carry it into every postcode in the land, so that they can do more.

"And, in doing more, build a new economy where we put life's essentials back under stronger public control to make them affordable to you again – reindustrializing Britain, using public procurement to back British industry."

Burnham, 56, was greeted by King Charles III at Buckingham Palace, London, on Monday before his swearing-in and first remarks. King Charles formally requested that Burnham form a new administration, and Burnham accepted.
WHO IS ANDY BURNHAM? THE TRUMP CRITIC SET TO BECOME THE UK'S NEXT PRIME MINISTER

Andy Burnham delivers his inaugural speech as the U.K.'s new prime minister on July 20, 2026, in London. He becomes the U.K.'s 59th prime minister, succeeding Sir Keir Starmer. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

"I have just come from Buckingham Palace, where I have accepted His Majesty the King's invitation to form a government," Burnham's brief introduction began. "And in doing so, I am acutely conscious that I am the sixth person in the last 10 years to walk up this street – the seventh prime minister since 2016, making this a moment for reflection and new resolution.

"It requires my generation of politicians to raise our game and rise to the new challenge. Britain needs to show the world that we can regain our stability once again, and that is our challenge to make politics work, to make it work better," he said.
"I know people at home are fed up with politics. I hear you and I want to be honest with you: We have not been good enough, and we need to be better. We will be."
Burnham called for sweeping political and economic changes.
UK PM ANDY BURNHAM REJECTS THATCHER-ERA POLICIES, SIGNALS LEFTWARD SHIFT

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham is welcomed by King Charles III during an audience at Buckingham Palace in London on Monday, July 20, 2026. Burnham was invited to become prime minister and form a new government. (PA Wire/PA Images)
"We will make this moment a circuit breaker for Britain, bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years," he said. "A new political model and a new economic model.
"In the 1980s, Britain took some wrong turns. Political power was centralized, economic power privatized, large parts of the country deindustrialized, and they still haven't recovered.
"Many feel as though they're still in decline, and they don't have the ability to turn things around."
Burnham vowed to "bring forward a new plan for Britain."

"A 10-year plan, laying out a path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be – wherever we're coming from, whatever party we support," he said. "But I can do something to give people some breathing space now, some help with the cost of living. And I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them.

"We will help more young people into work by changing the education system and giving them more support, more mental health support, and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down to meet our fiscal rules and to honor our commitments on defense to our international partners."
ANDY BURNHAM ELECTED LABOUR LEADER, SET TO BECOME UK PRIME MINISTER
Prime Minister Andy Burnham assumes the leadership role without being elected, a fact not lost on critics of his democratic-socialist agenda. (Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)
His first order of business in office will be "to end rough sleeping in our country."
"It's about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government," he concluded. "I will put the care of people at the heart of everything I do.

"I will give this my all and I ask you all to pull with me. Let's build a new national sense of unity, of common purpose and positivity. Let us make this the moment when Britain starts to believe again, the moment we bring back hope. Thank you very much, everybody."
Outgoing Keir Starmer officially submitted his resignation and passed "the baton" in remarks outside 10 Downing Street.
BRITISH PRIME MINISTER KEIR STARMER FACES POTENTIAL LEADERSHIP CHALLENGE FROM NEWLY-ELECTED ANDY BURNHAM

Outgoing Labor Prime Minister Keir Starmer bid farewell to office Monday morning outside 10 Downing Street: "As I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham, I wish him every success: He has my full support." (Carl Court/Getty Images)
"As I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham, I wish him every success," Starmer said. "He has my full support.

"For all the focus on individuals, politics will always be a team sport and the changes we have delivered for our country and our party belong to everyone who has fought for them. I thank them again today, and I thank the British people for the opportunity to serve.
"I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved."
STARMER IN 'SEISMIC' CRISIS, UK DEFENSE CHIEF QUITS BEFORE HIGH-STAKES TRUMP NATO SUMMIT

Burnham's relationship with Washington could provide an early foreign-policy test. He has repeatedly criticized Trump, comparing the instability surrounding the president’s return to office with the turmoil under former British Prime Minister Liz Truss and warning against importing what he called America’s polarized political culture.
He has maintained that the U.S.-U.K. relationship remains important, though, pledging continuity on NATO, Britain’s nuclear deterrent and support for Ukraine.

Trump previously dismissed Burnham as the former "mayor of a town" and said he had heard the incoming British leader was "extremely liberal." Reform UK has also challenged Burnham’s mandate, arguing that he should call a general election after reaching Downing Street without facing either a competitive Labor leadership contest or a nationwide vote.
KEIR STARMER REPORTEDLY CONSIDERING STEPPING DOWN AS PM AND COULD ANNOUNCE TIMETABLE FOR DEPARTURE

Burnham succeeds Starmer after becoming Labor leader unopposed Friday. He enters office without a new national vote under Britain’s parliamentary system, which allows the governing party to change leaders midterm. The next general election is not required until 2029, though Burnham could call one earlier.

At the center of his agenda is what he calls "Manchesterism" — an effort to give cities and regions greater authority over transportation, housing, infrastructure and economic development. He has paired that approach with what he describes as "business-friendly socialism," combining greater public control of essential services with cooperation between government and private industry.

Burnham's arrival at Downing Street caps a decade-long political comeback. After losing his second Labor leadership contest in 2015, Burnham left national politics and built a new power base in Greater Manchester, where nine years as mayor earned him the nickname "King of the North" and a reputation as an effective communicator willing to challenge the government in London.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I will work to build a new politics; the country is crying out for it," he said Friday. "People are looking for us to deliver, and we will."
Reuters and Fox News' Efrat Lachter contributed to this report.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Steve Forbes urges Trump to keep the Strait of Hormuz open at all costs
summary: Publisher Steve Forbes calls for maximum pressure on Tehran regime, urges Trump administration to keep the Strait of Hormuz open as a non-negotiable imperative.
story: Publisher Steve Forbes argues the Strait of Hormuz is a strategic asset that must remain open at all costs, advises Trump to keep all options on the table in dealing with Iran
Steve Forbes says the United States must double down on efforts to topple the Tehran regime, arguing that free passage through the Strait of Hormuz should remain a non-negotiable American imperative.

As the U.S. struck targets in Iran for a ninth consecutive day on Sunday, pressure on the Tehran regime continued to build. Speaking at Freedom Fest in Las Vegas, the chairman and editor-in-chief of Forbes and former presidential candidate sat down with Fox News Digital to discuss Iran and the Trump administration's foreign policy.
STEVE FORBES BACKS TRUMP'S MT. RUSHMORE WARNING ON COMMUNISM: 'HE'S RIGHT'
"Get Iran done with. No more fake ceasefires. Get rid of that evil regime," Steve Forbes said. (Fox News)

"Going back to Thomas Jefferson, a core foreign policy plank of the United States is freedom of the seas. Freedom of navigation got us into another war with Great Britain, the War of 1812," Forbes said.
"So we've been doing it for over two centuries. The Strait of Hormuz is an international waterway, just as the South China Sea is an international waterway. And so we must keep that open.

August 1804: Tracers arc in the sky as ships of the U.S. navy bombard Tripoli in an action against a ruler who supported the Tripolitan (Barbary) pirates. The pirates demanded protection money from all ships and the USA decided to go to war to release their hold on the area.  (MPI/Getty Images)
"No tolls, no restrictions, all ships of commerce should have free passage through it unmolested."

Forbes said that with proper application of air power, boots on the ground wouldn't be needed, but he would not discard that as an option, bringing the example of the engagement with the Barbary pirates, which brought freedom of navigation to the Mediterranean following the completion of the First Barbary War of 1805.
TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS
The U.S. military has been enforcing a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, even during the ceasefire. (U.S. Central Command)

"If we do things right in the air, that won't be necessary. But as we demonstrated with the Barbary pirates, sometimes you do need hand-to-hand combat. But again, with our great military and the great Israeli military, we should be able to bring this evil regime down and enable the elements in the Iranian army that want change to feel we're not going to pull the rug out from under them with another fake ceasefire. That we keep hammering away at this evil regime."
A container ship, right, and a cargo vessel are seen in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, June 17, 2026. (Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA via AP)
Ultimately, Forbes said freedom of navigation should be an international red line:

"So the key thing is, if you don't enforce these key principles of freedom of navigation, liberty, you're going to lose them. Ronald Reagan was right. Others have made the same observation. You have to preserve liberty each and every generation."
President Ronald Reagan gives a speech from the Oval Office of the White House. (Diana Walker/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Forbes said the time for diplomacy with Tehran has passed, and encouraged the Trump administration to ratchet up the pressure, while also praising a recent decision on Ukraine policy.

"Get Iran done with. No more fake ceasefires. Get rid of that evil regime. By the way, I'm delighted that he's saying he's going to give licensing for Patriot missiles to Ukraine. That'll bring a good result there."
