summary: Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., said she will run for a full term for the seat held by her late brother, Lindsey Graham, days after President Donald Trump said he urged her to jump into the race.
story: Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., said she will run for a full term for the seat held by her late brother, Lindsey Graham, days after President Donald Trump said he urged her to jump into the race.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Graham said in an interview with Fox News’ Sean Hannity that she will run in next month’s special primary election to appear on the November ballot.
“I’ve made a decision,” Graham said in a clip released on X. “I’m in.”

“I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family. But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey. He cared about the people of this state. I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state,” Graham said. “I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes, absolutely.”

Trump on Friday said that he had given his “complete and total endorsement” to Graham, the younger sister of the late senator. “I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

Graham was sworn in to the Senate seat last Tuesday, a day after South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to the role to finish out her late brother’s term, which ends in early January. The elder Graham died July 11 at age 71 of what was preliminarily diagnosed as a rupture of his aorta due to a hardening of his arteries, his office said.
Graham’s funeral services are scheduled for July 28 in Washington, D.C., and July 29 in South Carolina.

Other GOP candidates who have announced plans to run in the Aug. 11 election include South Carolina Republican Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman and South Carolina businessman Mark Lynch, who lost to Lindsey Graham in the June Republican primary.
Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., who ran an unsuccessful bid for South Carolina governor this year, said in a video statement Monday afternoon that she will not be seeking the Senate seat.

“I want to be straight with you. I’m not running for the U.S. Senate, not because I’m backing down from a fight, but because the one I’m already in matters now,” Mace said, referencing her legislative efforts on protecting women from sexual abuse.
“I’m not chasing another title, I’m chasing justice,” she added in her video, which was posted after Graham announced her candidacy.
The filing deadline for next month’s special election is July 28. The winner will go on to face Democrat Annie Andrews in November.
When she accepted her appointment to her brother’s seat last week, Darline Graham recounted their close relationship and said, “Lindsey has always been there for me, and now I will be there for him.”

title: FDA says it’s still investigating Taylor Farms in cyclosporiasis outbreak
summary: Taylor Farms continues to be the subject of a Food and Drug Administration investigation into the growing cyclosporiasis outbreak, despite a false positive test result, the agency said Monday.
story: Taylor Farms continues to be the subject of a Food and Drug Administration investigation into the growing cyclosporiasis outbreak, despite a false positive test result, the agency said Monday.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Late Sunday, the FDA said that a lettuce sample from the company had falsely tested positive for cyclospora, the parasite that causes the illness. That sample, however, did not come from lettuce already implicated in the outbreak and recall. Instead, it came from a separate shipment the agency collected during routine import inspections.

“To clarify, this false-positive lab sample DOES NOT change the basis for FDA’s ongoing outbreak investigation or the overwhelming epidemiological data supporting the current voluntary recall by Taylor Farms,” the FDA said Monday on X.
The company’s voluntary recall of shredded iceberg lettuce to 27 states is still in effect.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

On Sunday, Taylor Farms said in a statement that the FDA had “apologized” about the false positive test results. On a call Monday, an FDA official disputed Taylor Farms’ claim that the agency had issued an official apology.
Taylor Farms did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Determining the source of an outbreak goes beyond finding a positive sample.

Public health officials don’t rely solely on laboratory tests to identify the source of a foodborne outbreak, said Donald Schaffner, a food microbiology professor and chair of the food science department at Rutgers University.
Instead, investigators look at patient samples and interviews, food receipts and information from the food supply chain to determine where the contaminated food likely came from.

In the ongoing outbreak, investigators found that many people who got sick had eaten at Taco Bell restaurants supplied with Taylor Farms lettuce. As of Saturday, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention had confirmed more than 1,600 cases in people in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia.

“Taylor Farms is still implicated because of the epidemiology,” Schaffner wrote in an email. “This means that people that ate at Taco Bell, and ate Taylor Farm lettuce, are sick with the parasite. It’s important to realize that this is only a statistical correlation. Correlation is not causation, but it was strong enough evidence that FDA and CDC believe that this is the cause.”
On Saturday, Taco Bell said it had removed all Taylor Farms lettuce from its U.S. restaurants.
Schaffner said it’s unusual for investigators to be able to detect the cyclospora parasite in a food sample.
“Almost always it’s too late because the food has already spoiled or has been eaten,” he said.

A positive result for the parasite would have been a strong piece of confirmatory data, said Don Stoeckel, an environmental microbiologist and associate at the Produce Safety Alliance, a food safety training group.
The lack of a positive result, however, “does not reduce the importance of following the CDC’s recommendation to avoid consumption of the product named on the CDC investigations page,” Stoeckel said.

title: Judge pauses Paramount-Warner merger
summary: Twelve state attorneys general requested a temporary restraining order barring Paramount Skydance from closing the blockbuster deal.
story: Paramount Skydance’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery hit a roadblock Monday when a federal judge paused the proposed merger, granting a request from a coalition of 12 state attorneys general who sued to thwart the $110 billion deal.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín of the Northern District of California issued a temporary restraining order barring Paramount from closing the transaction, a corporate tie-up that would unite two movie studios, two streaming platforms and two news organizations under the control of David Ellison, the son of billionaire technology tycoon Larry Ellison.

Martínez-Olguín’s order said the restraining order will remain in effect for 14 days. The judge, who is presiding over the case, scheduled an Aug. 3 hearing on the states’ motion for a preliminary injunction, which would freeze the transaction while the legal process plays out.
The plaintiffs, led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, sued to block the merger July 13, arguing in a 38-page complaint that it would “extinguish competition” in Hollywood.

“The unlawful merger of these two entertainment behemoths would lead to higher prices, lower quality, and less content for film and television, harming movie theaters, basic cable distributors, and ultimately, audiences on every sofa and movie theater seat in the U.S.,” Bonta said in a statement accompanying the court filing.

Bonta and his fellow Democratic attorneys general contend that the transaction violates Section 7 of the Clayton Antitrust Act of 1914, a federal law that bars mergers likely to substantially lessen competition.
Paramount-Warner merger could affect entertainment options

The states argue the deal would reduce competition in three areas: wide-release theatrical film distribution, anticipated top-grossing movie distribution and the market for distributing basic cable channels to cable and satellite providers.

Paramount has forcefully pushed back on those claims, arguing that the states’ crusade is “wrong on both the facts and the law” and blasting the restraining order bid as “one of the weakest merger challenges in modern antitrust history.”

In response to a request for comment on the temporary restraining order, a Paramount spokesperson said in part: “We are confident the evidence will demonstrate that the state AGs’ antitrust arguments are without merit as their alleged markets and claims of anticompetitive effects are without any basis in modern market realities.”
The company has already received regulatory clearance from the Justice Department, and it has touted similar approvals from other countries, including Australia and China.

Paramount executives are motivated to close the deal soon. That’s partly because the company agreed to pay Warner Bros. shareholders a “ticking fee” of 25 cents a share each quarter if the transaction isn’t wrapped up by Sept. 30.
The potential penalty is worth more than $600 million per quarter.

Paramount owns a 114-year-old film studio, the Paramount+ streaming service, the CBS broadcast network and a suite of cable assets that includes MTV and Nickelodeon. Warner Bros. owns a 116-year-old film studio, the cable brands CNN and HBO and popular intellectual property such as the Batman and Superman franchises.

The state-driven lawsuit is the most significant threat to the deal since it was inked, though it is not the only hurdle standing in Paramount’s way. The European Union’s antitrust arm is reviewing the transaction, and the British culture secretary recently said she was “minded to intervene” in the deal, citing concerns about concentrated ownership of media enterprises.
The merger has also drawn opposition from organized labor and a group of consumers.

The Writers Guild of America filed its own antitrust suit, arguing that the deal would suppress members’ wages and shrink the number of available jobs. Separately, a group of consumers filed an antitrust suit focused on the harms of combining Paramount+ and HBO Max. (Martínez-Olguín denied the consumer plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction to freeze the merger.)

In the states’ antitrust case, California’s Bonta was joined by the attorneys general of Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico and Oregon. New York Attorney General Letitia James has said the merger “threatens to raise costs for consumers and put jobs and businesses nationwide at risk.”

The proposed deal has a political dimension. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is an ally of President Donald Trump. Trump has praised the Ellison family and publicly called for new ownership of CNN. “We’re trying to have CNN go in a normal path,” Trump recently told the network’s Jake Tapper in an on-air phone interview.
The younger Ellison has already embarked on sweeping changes at CBS News, hiring opinion journalist Bari Weiss to overhaul “60 Minutes” and the network’s evening news broadcast.

title: From The Sports Desk: Spain is the world champion
summary: An extra-time goal by Ferran Torres gave the Spaniards their second world title and the first since 2010.
story: An extra-time goal by Ferran Torres gave the Spaniards their second world title and the first since 2010. As for Lionel Messi, the legend failed to influence the game and bowed out of the tournament with a silver medal. But will this be his last World Cup appearance?
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
World Cup final
Spain dominated Argentina to win a one-sided World Cup final in which even Lionel Messi struggled to make an impact.
The Spanish players were crowned champions for the second time after Ferran Torres netted his first goal of the tournament in the first half of extra-time to secure a 1-0 victory.
“It was a goal scored by 47 million people,” Torres said, referring to Spain’s population.
But this was by no means a classic contest. Argentina has been criticized for its physical approach to the game, which saw them fail to register a single shot on target.
The defending champions managed to hold Spain to a draw in the regulation 90 minutes, which ended with combative midfielder Enzo Fernandez being sent off after a reckless challenge in injury time.
Tempers flared after the dismissal and again at the final whistle, with players from both sides and Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni involved in a heated confrontation.
In the end, Spain denied Messi a second consecutive World Cup title in what the 39-year-old has indicated will be the final World Cup appearance of his career.
Barcelona forward Torres, introduced in the second half, pounced on a loose ball in the penalty area and lashed a left-footed finish beneath the crossbar in the 106th minute.
From there, Spain’s suffocating defense did what it had done all tournament. The 2010 champions conceded just once in eight matches — the fewest goals ever allowed by a World Cup-winning team.
The team is now unbeaten in 38 matches — 29 wins and nine draws — the longest unbeaten run by any European men’s national team.
For more than two years, nobody has beaten Spain. Not even Messi.
“I feel pride, to be honest,” coach Luis de la Fuente said. “To accompany these players on this journey has been an honor.”
Argentina, which had made a habit of dramatic late comebacks throughout the tournament, could not find one more.

Messi’s final opportunity came from a corner with four minutes remaining of extra time. The ball broke kindly for substitute Giuliano Simeone, whose volley flew over the crossbar as he buried his head in disbelief.
“When you have Messi on the other side, you’re always nervous,” Torres said. “But we always trusted our football, and we showed it again.”

After the post-match confrontation, Spain’s players formed a guard of honor for Argentina as the runners-up walked to collect their medals from President Donald Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

For Messi, it was likely the final chapter of a remarkable World Cup career. He retired briefly after losing the 2016 Copa America final to Chile in the same stadium before reversing his decision weeks later.
The choice transformed his legacy. He led Argentina to the 2022 World Cup, won Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024, and claimed Argentina’s player of the year award 16 times across 19 years.
His place among football’s all-time greats is beyond question. But yesterday, Spain was simply better.
Bronze medal match
Bukayo Saka scored three goals as England beat France 6-4 to finish third at the World Cup on Saturday.
It was the highest-scoring World Cup match since Hungary’s 10-1 victory over El Salvador in 1982, while the 10 goals were the most ever in a third-place playoff.

Saka struck in the 37th minute and first-half stoppage time before completing his second England hat trick with an 87th-minute penalty. Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa also scored as England raced to a 4-0 halftime lead before surviving a frantic second half to secure the nation’s best World Cup finish since winning the title in 1966.
Jude Bellingham sealed the victory in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time with his seventh goal of the tournament.
Kylian Mbappé scored twice to take his World Cup tally to 10 goals, earning the Golden Boot as the tournament’s top scorer. His 22 career World Cup goals moved him one ahead of Messi.

France trailed 4-0 before Mbappé sparked a comeback attempt, flicking the ball past goalkeeper Dean Henderson in the 48th minute before adding a second with a left-footed finish from about 14 yards in the 66th.
It was the final match in charge for France coach Didier Deschamps, who is stepping down after 14 years. Deschamps embraced his players and waved to the crowd as he left the pitch.
A look back
The first 48-team World Cup delivered upsets, dramatic comebacks, spectacular goals and standout performances from the game’s biggest stars.
Here are some of the key takeaways from the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada.
Expanding the tournament from 32 to 48 teams prompted fears of one-sided matches and a diluted group stage. Instead, several newcomers emerged among the competition’s biggest stories.

Cape Verde drew with Spain in its opener, reached the round of 32 and pushed Argentina to extra time before losing 3-2 in one of the tournament’s best matches. Veteran goalkeeper Vozinha became an unlikely cult hero at 40, attracting millions of social media followers.
The Golden Boot race became a showcase for the sport’s biggest names.

Mbappé won the Golden Boot race after netting 10 goals, taking his career World Cup tally to a record 22. Messi showed why he is an icon of the sport, scoring eight in the tournament, taking his career total to 21 overall.
England stars Harry Kane and Bellingham were also among the leading scorers, and 6-foot-5 Norwegian striker Erling Haaland introduced himself to the American public with some superb displays.

title: Ismael ‘El Mayo’ Zambada, co-founder of El Chapo’s drug cartel, sentenced to life in U.S. prison
summary: Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, co-founder of El Chapo’s Sinaloa cartel, was sentenced to life in prison in Brooklyn federal court.
story: NEW YORK — Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, a founder of the Sinaloa cartel, was sentenced to life in prison in Brooklyn federal court, where he took responsibility in leading one of the world’s largest and most violent drug trafficking organizations.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

His life sentence closes a yearslong effort by the federal government to take down the infamous cartel leader who eluded the reach of U.S. law enforcement for decades. Zambada was arrested in 2024 after he claimed that he was kidnapped in Mexico and flown to Texas.
Along with a life sentence, he was also ordered to forfeit $15 billion, however prosecutors have yet to locate a bulk of the illicit profits.

Dressed in tan prison garb, Zambada appeared expressionless while he sat at the defense table in court on Monday. Speaking through a Spanish-language interpreter, he apologized, saying, “I am not here to ask for compassion. I am here to take responsibility and to say I’m sorry — for the harm I caused and for the example I set.”

“I grew up in an environment where violence and crime seemed normal, but now I know that’s no excuse,” said Zambada, who read from a prepared statement. “There comes a time when every person must take responsibility for their decisions. I didn’t, and many people paid the price.”

For decades, Zambada and co-founder Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán built the Sinaloa cartel into a prolific criminal enterprise defined by violence and corruption, flooding the U.S. with tons of cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine.
Guzmán was convicted in 2019 and is serving a life sentence at a federal prison in Colorado.

Zambada pleaded guilty last year to charges of engaging in a continuing criminal enterprise and racketeering conspiracy, acknowledging culpability for 85 underlying crimes. His change of plea was entered after the government said it wouldn’t seek the death penalty.

He acknowledged the scope of the Sinaloa operation, including underlings who built relationships with cocaine producers in Colombia, oversaw importing cocaine to Mexico by boat and plane and smuggling the drug across the U.S.-Mexico border. He said the cartel raked in hundreds of millions of dollars a year and admitted that people working for him paid hefty bribes to Mexican officials.

Frank Perez, an attorney for Zambada, said in court that his client didn’t cooperate with the government in a “typical sense,” adding that he didn’t divulge information about Sinaloa cartel members or Mexican government officials.

“During El Mayo’s reign, tens of thousands of parents lost their children to addiction, overdose, and drug-related violence. I hope that El Mayo’s life sentence brings some small measure of comfort to those families who have suffered unimaginable pain,” U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. told reporters outside of court.
He added, “The message today is clear: Drug dealing is a dead end, not just figuratively, but literally a dead end. Drug dealers die in prison.”

title: Here’s how often you should change your towels, and when to throw them away, according to experts
summary: I talked with laundry experts to learn how often you should change ans wash your towels and when it’s best to throw them away in exchange for new ones.
story: We don’t always have the answers, but we have some people on speed dial who do — which is why we present to you our series FYI where we have experts explain if lip balm is actually bad, how often should you wash your hair and more.

Having a few high-quality towels is a must when it comes to having a well-stocked bathroom. But even the most luxurious towels can end up in bad shape after years of use and hundreds of washes. While you probably wash your towels regularly, do you know if you’re changing them out frequently enough? And how long should you keep the same rotation of towels at home before buying a new set?

After just a few months, the texture and feel of towels deteriorate and even if you wash them, they sometimes don’t always smell fresh. To find out how often you should change your towels to wash them and when it’s time to consider buying a new set, I spoke with laundry experts for their guidance and recommendations.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
How often should you wash your towels?
You should change out and wash towels after every two to five uses to make sure they don’t get too soiled, according to Frej Lewenhaupt, the owner and CEO of clothing care company Steamery.

“It’s important to make sure you’re drying your bath towel fully in between each use to avoid bacteria and mildew growth, which can lead to an unpleasant smell,” he says. “A tip to ensure this is to rotate between two towels so they each get the chance to fully dry before the next use.”
With this in mind, you should always have at least two clean towels available throughout the week, particularly if you shower multiple times a day.
How often should you replace your towels?

While it depends on the quality of your towels and how often you use them, you should replace towels every two to four years, according to Salvador Villareal, the co-founder of laundry services company VIP Cleaners & Laundry.

“Replace them once they turn thin, rough, or permanently stained, or once they develop persistent odors or lose absorbency,” he says. It’s often easy to tell the difference between a fresh, brand new towel versus one that you’ve used and washed regularly for a few years because the texture often changes and, depending on how you launder them, they don’t always smell great even after a single wash. If it becomes hard to get that odor out on the first try, that’s probably a sign you should throw out the towel.
Should you wash a towel every time you use it?

You don’t necessarily have to wash your towel each time you use it — you can wash it after every two to five uses, as Lewenhaupt recommends above. With that said, this could change depending on things like how humid your bathroom is, how well you’re washing your towels when you do wash them and if they’re drying well in between uses.

As mentioned above, you should use at least two different towels at a time and alternate between them throughout the week. If they don’t have time to dry, they start to develop mildew, which causes unpleasant smells. So while you may not need to wash your towel after one use, you might want to swap it with a clean towel, which means you’d grab it after every other shower or bath.
What’s the best way to wash towels?

It’s best to wash towels separately from regular clothing with warm water, according to Villareal. “Go easy on fabric softener, it coats the fibers and cuts absorbency,” he says. “Use the recommended detergent amount and dry towels thoroughly before folding or storing.” Additionally, Villareal says that it’s a misconception that using more detergent gets clothing cleaner, when it really depends more on the technique and temperature you use.

title: Is the Oura Ring 5 worth it?
summary: The Oura Ring 5 is significantly smaller and slimmer than previous versions. But is it worth the upgrade? I tested it for over a month to find out.
story: The Oura Ring 5 is the best smart ring you can buy.  Full stop. Just like the Oura Ring 4 before it, it marries a great design, an intuitive app and accurate data in a small package. But that doesn’t mean it’s automatically the best fitness tracker for you. There are dozens of excellent alternatives, including smart rings like the RingConn Gen 3 and screen-free trackers like the Whoop 5.0 and Google Fitbit Air. With more competition than ever on the market you may be asking, is the Oura Ring 5 worth it?

I’ve been testing the Oura Ring for years, starting with the Oura Ring Gen 3. Now that I’ve spent more than a month using the Oura Ring 5, I can confidently say that it is the best smart ring the brand’s ever made: here’s everything you should know if you’re thinking about buying one.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
What is the Oura Ring 5?
Oura Ring 5
Smallest version yetGreat battery lifeAccurate health tracking
Smallest version yet
Great battery life
Accurate health tracking
Requires a subscription
Requires a subscription

The Oura Ring 5 is the brand’s newest smart ring. It tracks a plethora of health metrics, including heart rate, body temperature, respiratory rate, blood oxygen and more. It automatically detects and logs some exercise (mostly walks and runs), and lets you manually start and stop  any workout through the Oura app, where you can view all of your data.

The Oura Ring 5 is 40 percent smaller than the Oura Ring 4 — it’s a significant difference that’s quite noticeable to the wearer. It also gets slightly better battery life: six to nine days per charge (up from five to eight). It comes in six finishes and sizes range from six to 13 (the Oura Ring 4 comes in sizes four to 15).
The ring basically requires an Oura membership subscription ($5.99 per month or $69.99 per year), otherwise you’ll be limited to solely tracking the current day.
My experience with the Oura Ring 5

NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack and I wore the Oura Ring 5 for more than a month after receiving early samples from the brand to try out. I compared data from the Oura Ring 5 to other wearables like the Google Fitbit Air, Whoop 5.0 and Garmin watches. Cusack, who was trying the Oura Ring for the first time, focused on first impression and usability.
Much smaller and slimmer than past Oura Rings

I am not much of a ring person — I generally prefer watches and smartwatches to smart rings. The Oura Ring 4 didn’t change that, but the Oura Ring 5 came close. It’s significantly smaller and slimmer than the previous version, which made it much more comfortable to wear on a daily basis. I didn’t feel it clashing against everything I touched, squeezing against my adjacent fingers while washing my hands, or pushing against weights during strength straining nearly as much as previous iterations. That added comfort made wearing the ring much more enjoyable — most of the time, I forgot I even had it on.
Accurate sleep tracking

Oura Ring continues to have some of the best sleep tracking in a wearable. Like the Oura Ring 4 before it, it tracked my sleep more accurately than other options like my Apple Watch Series 11 and Google Fitbit Air. More often than not, it correctly logged sleep interruptions — I woke up a few times in the middle of the night to take care of my toddler during the test period, and the Oura Ring 5 usually logged these small wake windows accurately.
Accurate illness tracking (Symptom Radar)

Both Cusack and I fell sick during our testing period of the Oura Ring 5, and both of our rings confirmed illness through the symptom radar feature. Both of our symptom radars reported “Major signs of strain,” with elevated resting heart rate, body temperature and respiratory rates. This isn’t unique to the Oura Ring 5, but it continues to be a useful feature that can help remind you to take time to rest and recover when needed.

Cusack did find this interesting, but felt it was a bit stressful to see, especially the red color shift that goes along with the major signs text. I didn’t mind it so much, probably because I’ve tested so many fitness trackers.
It’s still not the best option for athletes

The Oura Ring 5 automatically tracks most health and sleep data very well. It isn’t so great at automatically tracking exercise, though. This isn’t unique to Oura, but it’s worth mentioning for anyone thinking the Oura Ring 5 will magically track any and all of your physical activity perfectly. It won’t. Outdoor cycling is a prime example: With automatic tracking, it botched all GPS-related data (distance, speed and mapping), but manually starting and stopping led to much more acceptable data.
It’s starting to feel like too much information

I’ve been testing the Oura Ring since the Oura Ring Gen3 launched in 2021. The ring’s capabilities, and the information the Oura Ring app shows you, have changed a lot in those few years. Things like sleep debt, symptom radar, heart health, metabolic health, health panels, glucose tracking and GLP-1 insights are all interesting features, but the more data, insights and capabilities Oura adds, the harder it becomes to make everything feel useful and holistic without being overwhelmed.
I still feel that Oura does this well, especially compared to other brands. But it’s a tension I am starting to become more and more aware of, especially compared to simpler (past) iterations.
Who is the Oura Ring 5 for?

The Oura Ring 5 is the best smart ring you can buy. The smaller size compared to the Oura Ring 4 is a big deal, and it’s much more comfortable to wear. The app provides useful, accurate health and sleep insights, organized in a mostly approachable way. It’s still not the best option for athletes or anyone doing outdoor fitness regularly — its data isn’t as accurate or useful as that of smartwatches or fitness trackers like the Apple Watch or Garmin Forerunner series.

Overall, I think anyone wearing an Oura Ring 4 shouldn’t feel the need to upgrade right away. While the smaller size is nice, the data and app experience is largely the same  — I’d wait until you start having issues with (or lose) your existing ring, or it gets marked down during a major sale.
Frequently asked questions

You can still find the Oura Ring 4 at select retailers, often for a lower price than the Oura Ring 5. Still, I would recommend the Oura Ring 5 to anyone new to the brand. Its slimmer size makes it much more comfortable to wear than the 4, so if you don’t already have one, it’s absolutely worth it to get this newest iteration over an older model.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who covers technology, fitness and outdoors, including stories on running shoes and wireless earbuds. For this piece, NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack and I wore the Oura Ring 5 for more than a month after the brand sent them to us to try. I tracked my daily stats, sleep and exercise and compared the data and fit and feel to previous Oura Rings and other wearables on the market.

title: Sen. Darline Graham says she is running for a full 6-year term after Trump urged her to jump into the race
summary: Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., said she will run for a full term for the seat held by her late brother, Lindsey Graham, days after President Donald Trump said he urged her to jump into the race.
story: Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., said she will run for a full term for the seat held by her late brother, Lindsey Graham, days after President Donald Trump said he urged her to jump into the race.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Graham said in an interview with Fox News’ Sean Hannity that she will run in next month’s special primary election to appear on the November ballot.
“I’ve made a decision,” Graham said in a clip released on X. “I’m in.”

“I’ve been praying a lot, talking to my family. But with the love of my family, with the support of his staff, I know I’m a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey. He cared about the people of this state. I’ve worked for almost 30 years for the people of this state,” Graham said. “I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes, absolutely.”

Trump on Friday said that he had given his “complete and total endorsement” to Graham, the younger sister of the late senator. “I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

Graham was sworn in to the Senate seat last Tuesday, a day after South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to the role to finish out her late brother’s term, which ends in early January. The elder Graham died July 11 at age 71 of what was preliminarily diagnosed as a rupture of his aorta due to a hardening of his arteries, his office said.
Graham’s funeral services are scheduled for July 28 in Washington, D.C., and July 29 in South Carolina.

Other GOP candidates who have announced plans to run in the Aug. 11 election include South Carolina Republican Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman and South Carolina businessman Mark Lynch, who lost to Lindsey Graham in the June Republican primary.
Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., who ran an unsuccessful bid for South Carolina governor this year, said in a video statement Monday afternoon that she will not be seeking the Senate seat.

“I want to be straight with you. I’m not running for the U.S. Senate, not because I’m backing down from a fight, but because the one I’m already in matters now,” Mace said, referencing her legislative efforts on protecting women from sexual abuse.
“I’m not chasing another title, I’m chasing justice,” she added in her video, which was posted after Graham announced her candidacy.
The filing deadline for next month’s special election is July 28. The winner will go on to face Democrat Annie Andrews in November.
When she accepted her appointment to her brother’s seat last week, Darline Graham recounted their close relationship and said, “Lindsey has always been there for me, and now I will be there for him.”

title: Trump says new Air Force One will be sent away for upgrades, amid security concerns
summary: President Trump said the Air Force One plane that was donated by Qatar will be sent away for upgrades, amid swirling concerns about its security features.
story: President Donald Trump said the new Air Force One plane that was gifted by Qatar will be sent away for upgrades, amid swirling concerns about its security features.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
As he returned from a trip to the FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey on Sunday, Trump was asked by reporters whether the plane lacked missile-defense capabilities.

“It has a lot of capability,” Trump said of the jet, which he started using this month. “But as I understand it, in about a month ​or so, they’re gonna send it to have it be maxed out ... It’ll take about ​a month,” Trump added. He did not detail the nature of the work.
Trump’s decision to fly back from a NATO summit in Turkey in a different presidential aircraft made headlines earlier this month.
The decision to ditch the Qatari-donated jet set off speculation about why the administration made the switch and the readiness of the new Air Force One.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement Monday that Trump will fly on the old Air Force One as the new one is upgraded.

“The new Air Force One is perfectly safe for the President’s travels, but will receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete,” Leavitt said.

A senior administration official said that the plan is for the plane to receive the “additional upgrades” in September, but it’s unclear whether that would come before or after Trump’s planned trip to the Irish Open at his golf resort in Doonbeg. The hope, according to the official, was to take the plane to Ireland first, as it is still considered safe for domestic travel and travel to Europe.

Earlier this month, Trump denied that security concerns were part of the decision to use the old Air Force One when departing from Turkey. But he said, “You know the life of a president is very dangerous,” and he added later: “I’m No. 1 on the kill list for Iran.”

NBC News reported that the Secret Service urged Trump to take the old plane home from Turkey because he was departing from a location near the Middle East and the U.S. had just resumed hostilities with Iran.
Why Trump was advised to not use Qatari-gifted Air Force One plane
Four New York Times journalists were subpoenaed by the Justice Department this month, after writing stories about security concerns involving the new Air Force One.
The superluxury Boeing 747-8 jumbo jet was gifted by the Qatari royal family last year to be used by Trump as the new Air Force One.
In June, Trump welcomed its delivery in an appearance at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington.

Decked out in a red, white and dark blue color scheme — a departure from the lighter blue on the previous model — Trump called it a “flying White House at a level of luxury no one has ever seen before,” adding “nobody tops this one.”
He flew on it to North Dakota on July 1 during a museum event honoring President Theodore Roosevelt.
The ornate jet is meant to serve as a temporary replacement as Boeing works on delivering long-delayed next-generation Air Force One planes expected in 2028.
