title: Does ‘The Odyssey’ Have an End Credits Scene?
summary: Does The Odyssey have an end credits scene? Here’s what to know about the ending of The Odyssey and what happens next.
story: Warning: This contains spoilers for the end of “The Odyssey.”
For nearly three hours, “The Odyssey” takes theatergoers on an epic journey.

The highly anticipated film was a hit at the box office in its first weekend of release, with the tale of Odysseus (Matt Damon) from one of the most celebrated works of literature in world history captivating movie fans to the tune of $264.1 million in ticket sales worldwide.

Packed with Hollywood stars like Damon, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Tom Holland, Lupita Nyong’o, Charlize Theron and Robert Pattinson, the movie has brought director Christopher Nolan’s vision of the ancient Greek epic to life and debuted to rave reviews.
“For me to take on Greek mythology on a big modern cinematic canvas is something that hasn’t been done,” Nolan told Kaylee Hartung on TODAY July 17.

A staple of many modern blockbusters has been an extra post-credits scene rewarding moviegoers who stick around until the absolute end. They have become a fixture in superhero and animated movies, popping up in “Masters of the Universe,” “Superman,” “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” and “Moana 2” among recent big films.
But when the credits roll on the nearly three-hour long “Odyssey,” is there one more scene at the end? Here’s what to know.
Is There a Post-Credits Scene at the End of ‘The Odyssey’?

No, once the swords-and-sandals epic has wrapped up after its 172-minute run time, that’s the end. There’s no secret scenes of Odysseus (Matt Damon) and his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) starting a new life in Los Angeles or anything.
Director Christopher Nolan had certainly done enough without needing any extra scenes, considering “The Odyssey” took three painstaking months to shoot all on 70-millimeter IMAX film.

“I definitely hit the limits of my own stamina and everybody’s stamina, I think. I mean, it’s ‘The Odyssey,’ of course it should be difficult,” he said on TODAY. “We’re not doing the job right making a film of ‘The Odyssey’ if it doesn’t seem difficult.”
So What Does Happen at the End of ‘The Odyssey’?
You would think there doesn’t need to be a spoiler alert for a story that was composed more than 2,000 years ago, but Nolan did put his own twist on the ending that differs from Homer’s epic poem.

In Nolan’s version, Odysseus and Penelope leave their son Telemachus (Tom Holland) behind and sail west toward the setting sun (probably not to Los Angeles). Odysseus is exiled, but he is with his beloved wife, who dreamed they would sail off together when news of the Trojan War first broke out.

In Homer’s version, the gods have much more of a say in how the story ends. Odysseus and Telemachus are about to battle all the angry families of Penelope’s suitors in Ithaca after Odysseus murdered all the wannabe husbands. However, the gods intervene.
“Zeus hurls a thunderbolt, and Athena makes them swear a truce,” Celsiana Warwick, assistant professor in the University of Iowa Department of Classics, tells TODAY.com.
Odysseus also isn’t done appeasing the gods, as the seer Tiresias tells Odysseus earlier in the poem that he must make a sacrifice to Poseidon in order to lift Poseidon’s curse on him.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Ending Explained: Christopher Nolan’s Movie Rewrites the Poem in This 1 Way
summary: What happens at the end of the Odyssey? What happens next for Odysseus? This is Christopher Nolan’s twist and what the myth says.
story: Warning: This contains spoilers for the end of “The Odyssey.”
You might have read “The Odyssey” before, but Christopher Nolan’s rendering of the epic poem, part of the Homeric cycle, offers up a brand new experience.

That’s especially true of the ending. Nolan reimagines what happens when Odysseus, played by Matt Damon, returns to Ithaca after 10 years fighting in the Trojan War and another 10 years trying to return to his kingdom.
Here’s what to know about Nolan’s twist on the ending of “The Odyssey,” how the real poem ends and the surprising, and unofficial, continuation of Odysseus’ story.
What Happens at the End of Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’?
Nolan’s “Odyssey” will be unfamiliar for those who read the epic poem.
It’s a bittersweet ending for Odysseus and his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway). After murdering the suitors who had been trying to court her, Odysseus is exiled from Ithaca.

He and Penelope leave their son Telemachus (Tom Holland) behind and sail west toward the setting sun, which is what Penelope dreamed they’d do when news of the Trojan War first broke out. Yes, he’s exiled — but at least they’re together.

Odysseus also reckons with the dire outlook for civilization at large and his role in it. Odysseus feels that the invasion of Troy broke “Zeus’ law,” cited throughout the movie — the code of conduct that says you should treat hosts and guests well, because anyone could be a god. The Trojan Horse, an act of war disguised as a gift, was a breach of the code.

Odysseus feels that this has led to the collapse of civilization. The “sea people,” spoken of throughout the movie with fear, are the returning Greek soldiers sacking towns, and spreading the violence that started in Troy.
He references the idea of oral history, which is how “The Odyssey” and its companion story “The Iliad” began. When people can no longer read, they will tell the stories of Troy in poems.

Scholar Joel Christensen, editor of “The Oxford Critical Guide to Homer’s Odyssey,” points out that Damon’s Odysseus does something Homer’s Odysseus doesn’t: Spares some of the suitors’ lives. He says Damon’s Odysseus is more of a “good guy” than the original.
“What I wanted to happen because it would have been more true to the poem is for him to kill the kneeling men,” Christensen says.
What Happens at the End of Homer’s ‘The Odyssey’?
“The ending of ‘The Odyssey’ is kind of strange,” Celsiana Warwick, assistant professor in the University of Iowa Department of Classics, tells TODAY.com.
The Hollywood version of the story might end with Penelope and Odysseus’ reunion. But that would have been “unsatisfying” to an ancient audience, Warwick says.

Instead, Odysseus has to face consequences for murdering all of the suitors, which compromise an elite swath of Ancient Greece’s population. The families of the suitors swarm Ithaca, wanting to get revenge on Odysseus and Telemachus. They’re about to rush into battle when the gods intervene. “Zeus hurls a thunderbolt, and Athena makes them swear a truce,” Warwick says.
Warwick adds that the ending speaks to an element of Greek culture during the archaic period “where blood feuds between aristocratic families could get way out of hand.”
“That’s something that would have been of great interest to an ancient audience, perhaps not so much to a modern audience,” she says.

Odysseus’ wandering continues, too, though his departure from Ithaca is not actually depicted in “The Odyssey.” Earlier on in the poem, the seer Tiresias tells Odysseus what he must do after killing the suitors.

In order to lift Poseidon’s curse, Odyssey has to take an oar and go on a journey until he finds men who don’t recognize it and know nothing of the sea. There, he will make a sacrifice to Poseidon, and all will be well. Tiresias predicted he would die of old age.
Jonathan Burgess, Emeritus professor of Classics, University of Toronto, calls the poem’s ending a “happy” one.

“There’s the recognition that things will follow. Poseidon’s still mad, but in the underworld, Odysseus was told how to stop Poseidon from being angry at him. There’s another adventure coming, but it’s a solution to anger from the divinity Poseidon — something you don’t want to hang over your life,” he says.
What Happens to Odysseus After ‘The Odyssey’?

“The Odyssey” ends with the gods intervening in a suitors’ battle. However, there’s more about Odysseus to be found in “other epics about the Trojan War and what happens after the Trojan War,” Burgess says.

“These existed apparently around the same time as ‘The Iliad’ and ‘The Odyssey.’ Same meter, same kind of poetry, same tradition. They told the whole story, starting from Paris and Helen to the sack of Troy,” Burgess says.
Unlike “The Iliad” and “The Odyssey,” these poems don’t exist in full. Instead, only fragments survived. Proclus, a Roman grammarian, wrote down summaries.
“The cycle poems were valued as context for Homer, but the poems themselves were not valued enough to be sung or to be preserved by the Roman period,” Burgess says.

The epic cycle concludes with “The Telegony,” which is about what happened after Odysseus’ homecoming. Author Madeline Miller looked to “The Telegony” for her popular book “Circe,” about the witch who hosts Odysseus during “The Odyssey.”
“The Telegony” is about Telegonus, the son Odysseus had during his time with Circe. Telegonus is not mentioned in “The Odyssey.”
He goes out in search of his father, carrying weapons from his mom — one being a poison-tipped spear. Eventually, he uses that spear on his father.
“Telegonus has never seen Odysseus. Odysseus has never seen Telegonus. Odysseus assumes he’s some stranger trying to steal his cattle. So they fight, and Telegonus kills his dad,” Burgess says.
Then comes something, perhaps, even stranger. First, Telegonus and Telemachus bring the corpse of Odysseus back to Aeaea, the island of Circe, and bury the body.
“Some people say Circe married Telemachus, and that Telegonus married Penelope. So there’s this strange two new weddings at the end of ‘The Telegony,’” Burgess says.

Burgess says Odysseus also remarries, according to certain myths. After leaving Ithaca to make a sacrifice for Poseidon, he travels to Epirus in northwest Greece. He married Callidice and has a son, Polypoetes, Burgess shares. After Callidice dies, he returns to Ithaca — setting the scene for “The Telegony.”
“The Telegony” place in relation to “The Odyssey” remains a mystery.
“Clearly, ‘The Telegony’ knows of ‘The Odyssey,’ but does ‘The Odyssey’ know of ‘The Telegony’”? Warwick asks.
She thinks “The Telegony” might speak to the idea of tying up loose ends.
“I think it is meant to be a happy ending. This is a way for his family to be happy without him,” Warwick says.

title: Marcello Hernández Goes Off-Script on TODAY, Leaving Al and Sheinelle in Shambles
summary: Marcello Hernández’s impression of Kevin Hart on TODAY left Sheinelle Jones and Al Roker in tears from laughing so much.
story: Hernández plus Hart equals hilarity.

Marcello Hernández and Kevin Hart, who star in the upcoming Netflix comedy “72 Hours,” stopped by TODAY July 20 for an interview that went off the rails when the “Saturday Night Live” star did an impression of the veteran comedian.
Things were already a bit goofy when Sheinelle Jones asked Hernández what it was like working with Hart.
“Do you want to see it? Should I show you?” he replied. “This is what it’s like to work with Kevin Hart.”
Hernández then launched into an impression of Hart on set, telling Sheinelle to pretend to be him asking Hart for advice.
“I’m sorry,” Hernández, fully in character as Hart, said, cutting her off while acting like he was on a phone call.

“They gotta bring the money up!” he said. “Money’s gotta be up if you want me to do that. Listen, I’m good. I’m good, but it’s gonna cost ya! I’m good. I know what I’m doing. Yeah, I’ll be there ... for a price!”
Sheinelle and Hart doubled over in laughter, while the TODAY crew could be heard cackling in the background.
“Add a zero!” Hernández said.
“This is ridiculous,” Hart said in response to the impression.
“No, it’s not,” Hernández fired back, while pointing out that Hart had AirPods behind him.
He joked Hart had the earbuds “just in case a CEO calls and is like, ‘We want Kevin to be the face of Froot Loops.’”
Sheinelle continued to howl, while the camera cut away to Al Roker, who was also doubling over in laughter.
Hernández finally broke character and gushed about Hart.
“I’m grateful to work with Kevin,” he said. “He’s a nice guy.”
Hart returned the kind words.
“I got to witness this in real time. But he is exactly what you would think that he is,” he said, adding that his co-star did “an amazing job” hosting the 2026 ESPY Awards.
Hernández wasn’t quite finished poking fun at Hart, teasing him about his shirt.

“Kevin is waking up in the morning going, ‘Which shirt should I wear? Should I wear a normal shirt, like a human being, or should I put on this weird rust-silver combo? Looks like I’m golfing, but also I’m the maître d’ at a steakhouse,’” he joked.
“Why don’t you ever wear socks? How about we talk about that?” Hart fired back.
“Because I’m Dominican,” Hernández said.
The whole interaction was just too much for Sheinelle.
“I can’t, I can’t,” she said as the interview drew to a close. “I don’t even need to say anything else.”
She then tossed to Al for the weather.
“Add another zero to the temperature,” Al joked, drawing laughs.

title: How to Watch the World Cup Final, Including Closing Ceremony and Halftime Show
summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup final takes place July 19 between TEAM and TEAM. It will include a star studded closing ceremony and halftime show.
story: The 2026 FIFA World Cup championship takes place July 19 at the New York New Jersey Stadium, better known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The tournament’s final game between reigning champion Argentina and Spain will make history by featuring the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show, an 11-minute extravaganza co-headlined by pop superstars Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira and BTS, among others.
For the latest World Cup info, follow TODAY.com’s liveblog
A star-studded closing ceremony will celebrate the tournament’s 48 teams from around the world with performances by Post Malone, Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams, Laura Pausini and IShowSpeed.
Tom Cruise will also make a special appearance during the closing ceremony. EGOT winner Jennifer Hudson will be on hand to perform the United States national anthem just ahead of the game.
Mexico, Canada and the U.S. hosted nearly 100 matches across venues in 16 cities, making the 2026 World Cup the biggest ever.
Read on to learn how to watch the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
When Does the 2026 World Cup Closing Ceremony Start?

The 2026 World Cup’s closing ceremony now starts at 1:30 p.m. ET on July 19, ahead of the final championship match at New York New Jersey Stadium, also known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
The closing ceremony will feature performances by Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams, Laura Pausini and IShowSpeed.
Oscar winner Tom Cruise will also make a special appearance and EGOT winner Jennifer Hudson will sing the U.S. national anthem.
When Does the Match Start?
The 2026 World Cup’s final match kicks off at 3 p.m. ET.
Who Will Perform at the 2026 FIFA World Cup  Final Halftime Show?
This year’s World Cup features the tournament’s first-ever halftime show.
Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira and BTS will co-headline the 11-minute show.
Burna Boy, Gustavo Dudamel and PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay are also set to perform.
How Can I Watch the 2026 World Cup Final?
Soccer fans in the U.S. can tune into the 2026 FIFA World Cup final live on FOX and in Spanish on Telemundo.
The tournament’s final can also be streamed live on Peacock, FOX Sports, YouTube TV and Fubo.

title: Xzibit Shares He Still Has The Same Beloved Cat From His ‘Pimp My Ride’ Days
summary: “Pimp My Ride” host Xzibit shared in a social media post on July 16 that Thunder Cat, a cat that he’s had since 2006, is still with him to this very day.
story: Be still our millennial hearts.
Rapper Xzibit shared in a social media post on July 16 that Thunder Cat, a pet that he’s had since 2006, is still with him to this very day.
As many a millennial has pointed out, that means that Xzibit has had his buddy with him since his days, hosting popular MTV show “Pimp My Ride,” which ran from 2004 to 2007.

People were more than impressed with Thunder Cat’s longevity. And with the show centered around turning banged up cars into impressive, often-outrageously upgraded rides, social media users couldn’t help but have a little fun.

“Yo dawg we heard you like cats so we put a litter box and a scratching post in your ‘03 Lincoln Navigator. We call it ‘Navigato’,” one Instagram user commented, mimicking Xzibit’s iconic lines on the show.
Others parodied the show’s theme song.
“🎶 So you wanna be a cool cat? But your kitty ain’t fly? You gotta hit me up because I’m a pretty cool guy ….It’s ya boy X to Z XZibit!” a social media user wrote.
And many others pointed out how Thunder Cat has lived through quite a bit, with one Instagram user writing, “Thunder Cat’s been judging people since MySpace.”

“Pimp My Ride” lasted for six seasons. It cemented the rapper as an iconic MTV television host as he helped hopelessly unskilled drivers turn their vehicles into “pimped out” masterpieces with the experts at auto repair shop West Coast Customs.
The modifications were often just plain wild, as Xzibit would surprise participants with add-ons like a mobile CAT scan machine, a slot machine and a snow cone machine.
Netflix attempted an eight-episode reboot of the show entitled “Resurrected Rides” in 2024. But it was hosted by “SNL” alum Chris Reed rather than Xzibit.
The rapper was so touched by the excitement over Thunder Cat from fans, he posted a follow-up photo on July 18 with the little lady.
“Yall made the last Thunder Cat post go viral,” Xzibit wrote on Instagram. “So she got a battery in her back acting like she ready to have her own s---… 🤦🏽‍♂️”

title: Justin Bieber, Shakira, BTS and More Performing at 2026 World Cup Final Closing Ceremony and Halftime Show
summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will continue to make history during the final match between reigning champs Argentina and Spain at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19.
story: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will continue to make history during the final match between reigning champs Argentina and Spain at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19.
This year’s World Cup was the first to feature three host countries: Mexico, United States and Canada.

Now, the global soccer tournament is having its first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show, featuring star-studded performances. Superstars like Shakira and Madonna, among other big names, will join forces as the co-headliners of the 11-minute halftime show.
For the latest World Cup info, follow TODAY.com’s liveblog
The 2026 World Cup final, which will see Spain take on reigning champions Argentina will also include a closing ceremony designed to honor the tournament’s 48 teams from around the world.
The closing ceremony will also feature special performances from stars like Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams and Jennifer Hudson, among others.
Tom Cruise is set to make a special appearance during the closing ceremony, which begins an hour and a half before the final kickoff.
Read on to learn more about the 2026 World Cup’s closing ceremony and halftime performance.
Who Is Performing During the Closing Ceremony?
The final game of the 2026 FIFA World Cup takes place July 19 at New York New Jersey Stadium, better known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The match will feature a closing ceremony celebrating the tournament’s global spirit with performances by Post Malone, Tony winner and Pussycat Doll singer Nicole Scherzinger, British pop star Robbie Williams, Italian pop star Laura Pausini and American streamer and musician IShowSpeed.
Oscar winner Tom Cruise will make a special appearance during the closing ceremony, which begins at 1 p.m. ET, an hour and a half before the game’s kickoff at 3 p.m. ET.
Who Will Perform the National Anthem?
Jennifer Hudson will be on hand to sing the U.S. national anthem just before the match.
Who Is Performing at Halftime?
This year’s championship game will be the first in FIFA World Cup history to feature a halftime performance of this caliber.
Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira and BTS will co-headline the 11-minute extravaganza.

Nigerian singer Burna Boy — whose current hit with Shakira, “Dai Dai,” is a 2026 World Cup anthem — will also take the stage along with Los Angeles Philharmonic director Gustavo Dudamel and New York City’s PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay.
How Can I Watch the 2026 World Cup Final?
Fans can watch the 2026 FIFA World Cup final live on FOX and in Spanish on Telemundo.
The match between Argentina and Spain can also be streamed live on Peacock, FOX Sports, YouTube TV and Fubo.

title: Burns, Bleach, Blindness: John Leguizamo Details Hair and Makeup Routine Behind His ‘Horrific’ ‘Odyssey’ Transformation
summary: Actor John Leguizamo reveals the bleach, the burns and the “severe emotional breakdowns” he underwent during the filming of the blockbuster movie “The Odyssey.”
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

If you look closely, you can spot John Leguizamo sporting a red track suit in the background of Madonna’s 1984 video, “Borderline.” It’s one of many under-fives the scrappy young comedian took along the way to Hollywood success.
A veteran of stage, film and television, Leguizamo’s resume is a  roundup of notable movies including “Moulin Rouge!” “Encanto” and “Ice Age,” as well as TV dramas like “ER” and “When They See Us.”

But it’s his latest role as Eumaeus, loyal servant to Odysseus (played by Matt Damon), in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster “The Odyssey” that Leguizamo, who turns 66 on July 22, says is the “highlight of my life.”
Even so, the actor reveals that over the months he shot the film, he was bleached, burned and, at times, emotionally broken.

Charming and dangerously funny, Leguizamo sat down in TODAY’s Orange Room to unpack it all, including why he was afraid to be left alone on the set of “The Odyssey” and the reason he gave his canine co-star, Argus, an NSFW nickname.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Star Tom Holland’s Quip About His Marriage To Castmate Zendaya Is Simply Epic
summary: Tom Holland joined Wired for an interview with his fellow “Odyssey” castmates Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway and Robert Pattinson and made a rare comment about his marriage to Zendaya.
story: When it comes to his love life, “The Odyssey” star Tom Holland doesn’t play.
Holland, who plays Telemachus, the son of main character Odysseus, joined Wired for an interview released on July 16 with fellow castmates Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway and Robert Pattinson.
When asked whether Athena — played by his beau Zendaya —loves Odysseus romantically, Holland had a quick response.
“No, because she’s married to me,” Holland said.
Damon, who plays titular character Odysseus, praised the swift retort.
“Good answer,” Damon said in the interview.

Holland, 30, and Zendaya, 29, have been famously private about their relationship. But when it comes to “The Odyssey,” directed by Christopher Nolan, Zendaya has been open about some special moments she’s had with Holland in regards to the film.

Zendaya told the AP that Holland had the chance to break the news of her casting. She said that her husband, who at the time had already been cast in the film, had just been coming home from a meeting with Nolan. She said that he handed her the film’s script, which the two had been reviewing together just the night before.
“He was like, ‘Read it again.’ And I was like, ‘OK,’” Zendaya, recalled to the AP. “And he was like, ‘But now, think of Athena.’”
It was then that Zendaya said she understood what was going on.
“I was like, ‘Stop right now! You’re joking!’” she told the AP.

title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Star Juno Temple Had a Hilarious, Full Circle Keeley Moment During the World Cup
summary: Juno Temple had a moment straight out of “Ted Lasso,” she tells TODAY.com. She also shares her World Cup highlights and best moments.
story: Juno Temple recently experienced a full circle moment during the World Cup.

During one of her recent hotel stays, she turned on the “telly,” only to witness one of her own commercials. “Ted Lasso” fans can recall that in the first season, Temple’s character Keeley, the spunky and ambitious model-turned-PR-marketing pro, sees herself promoting Liverpool on the hotel television.

“I was just in LA for a brief moment in time, and I actually got to stay at the Sunset Tower Hotel, and the Chase commercial was playing when you turn the telly on,” she tells TODAY.com. “And I was like, ‘Oh my god, that’s me! Oh, my god! ... That’s never happened to me before. I had a total moment.”
Temple described the moment as “crazy,” adding that life played out in a way that mirrored the commercial scene in the show.
“It legitimately happened to me!” Temple says.

Temple stars in a Chase Sapphire Reserve campaign that celebrates the summer of soccer. It also includes football player Myles Garrett and Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim. In the spot, Temple helps the couple learn more about soccer, (or, how it’s known around the world, “football”), demystifying the sport for American audiences.
Thanks to her “Ted Lasso” ties, Temple has gotten to learn more about the global sport and even had the opportunity to attend Argentina’s 3-1 win against Switzerland at the July 11 World Cup match.
Below, in her own words, Temple shares her favorite World Cup memories, highlights and more.

Oh boy, they would all be a bit blurred now because it’s always through my brothers. Truthfully, my brothers are the diehard football fans, so I just like being around (them). So anytime they want to watch a game, I’ll sort of tap in and tap out with them. But my earliest World Cup memory, I genuinely don’t actually remember it. It’s just always a part of (our lives).
I remember one when I was in New York and it was playing a lot, and I remember just everybody being on the streets of New York. But that would have been a few years ago now.

We got to go to a game, which was insanely exciting. I got to take my little brother, who is a football fanatic, and we got to see Argentina play Switzerland. (It was) honestly iconic, especially getting to watch my brother watch (Lionel) Messi play. He was wearing a Messi shirt and I did a sneaky thing where I filmed the back of his shirt, and then I zoomed in on the real Messi, and I sent it to him.

I got to do this thing with the Chase team this year, where we got to go and have dinner on the pitch, which was so crazy because I’ve never actually been out onto a football pitch before, let alone to have dinner. And it was right after America had played. This was in San Francisco, and when you see the scale of the pitch, and you’re aware of how big that space is, and just how active all the players are in that space for that length of time, I was like, “This is insane!” That honestly blew my mind. That was a pretty incredible experience.
(Between) taking my brother to the game and (the dinner), this will be a World Cup I will never forget. Is all I’m gonna say. This World Cup will be one ingrained in my memory for eternity.

There’s a quote about a hair dryer. I’m gonna look it up because I honestly had no idea what it would have meant at all. OK, here we go. “The ‘hair dryer treatment’ is a famous football cliche describing a manager that’s fiercely shouting at a player or a team in close quarters.”

And then on top of that, at the dinner on the pitch, Rio Ferdinand was the other guest there and it was his coach, (Alex Ferguson) that had actually coined that term! And I was like, “Oh my god, oh my god!” So that’s the first thing that comes to mind.
And then the second thing is just actually going out onto a pitch and seeing the size of the space that the players are playing on.

title: Will Ferrell, Amy Poehler Reflect On Making A ‘Flop’ Together: ‘Did Not Resonate At All’
summary: Will Ferrell joined Amy Poehler for a recent episode of her podcast “Good Hang with Amy Poehler” and the two took reflected on their work with one another including the 2017 film “The House.”
story: Will Ferrell and Amy Poehler have cemented their statuses as comedy icons. But even they have some, er, less well-received projects in their bodies of work.

Ferrell joined Poehler for a recent episode of her podcast “Good Hang with Amy Poehler” and the two took a trip down memory lane, reflecting on their work with one another including the 2017 film “The House.” While the comedy did not become the hit they had hoped, the pair both agreed that making the movie was a positive experience.
“We did ‘The House’ together, which was so fun to do with you,” Poehler said during the episode, which was released on July 14. “It was a dream come true to make a movie with you.”
Poehler added that it was a “flop.”
Ferrell admitted that the film “did not resonate at all.”
“Yet, I still argue that that movie’s funny,” said Ferrell, who stars in the new Netflix show “The Hawk.”
While the pair seems to have no regrets over the film, Poehler said that her kids never let her live it down.
“My kids often tell me — they’re like, ‘Mom, that was 7% on Rotten Tomatoes,’” Poehler said.

“The House” revolves around couple Scott and Kate Johansen, played by Ferrell and Poehler respectively, who start an illegal casino in their friend’s house to make enough money for their daughter’s college tuition. The film boasted a star-studded cast that included Nick Kroll, Rob Huebel and Jason Mantzoukas.
For the record, the movie has a 20% score on Rotten Tomato’s Tomatometer as of July 18.

Ferrell and Poehler have also had success together, namely with the 2007 ice-skating comedy “Blades Of Glory.” Both acknowledged during the podcast episode that they had to learn how to ice skate for the movie — something that Poehler wasn’t too happy about.
“I didn’t love it,” Poehler, who played villain Fairchild Van Waldenberg, said of ice skating. “I thought I’d be better at it and I was like, ‘F---, I’m not.’”

Ferrell, who played bad boy protagonist Chazz Michael Michaels, didn’t develop much of a hobby for the sport, either. He admitted during the podcast that he no longer ice skates. He does, however, still have some mementos from the movie.
“I have the skates packed away somewhere,” he said. “They were custom-made skates.”
Ferrell also told Poehler that he still owns the iconic fiery bodysuit made famous by the character.
“I have my costume. Framed,” Ferrell said, laughing. “It’s hanging in the garage but (wife Viveca Paulin) won’t let it come into the house.”

title: Lionel Messi Finally Addresses Iconic Photo Of Him Bathing Baby Lamine Yamal: ‘It’s Craziness’
summary: After photos went viral of Argentina star Lionel Messi bathing a baby Lamine Yamal of Spain, Messi opened up about the throwback snaps at a recent event in New York City as the two are slated to face off at the World Cup finals on July 19.
story: For weeks, World Cup fans have been abuzz about the now-iconic, throwback photos of Argentina star Lionel Messi bathing a baby Lamine Yamal, who’s now one of the best players from Spain. With the two now slated to face off on the pitch at the upcoming World Cup finals on July 19, as their countries vie for the championship, Messi recently addressed the remarkable snaps.
Speaking in front of a crowd at Fanatics Fest in New York City on July 17, Lionel Messi described the photos, taken in 2007 by photographer Joan Monfort as part of a charity calendar, as “crazy.”

“That photo is crazy because, well, it’s life,” Messi, speaking in Spanish, told NFL legend Tom Brady during the event. “I had a photo with him when he was a baby and for us to be facing each other in the World Cup. … It’s craziness.”
Messi marveled at the snaps, calling the 19-year-old Yamal “one of the best in the world at the moment, without a doubt.”

In the photos, which Messi took while on his then-club FC Barcelona, a soapy Yamal is just a couple months old. At the time, Messi, now a soccer legend, was a 20-year-old up-and-comer, making a name for himself with the club.
Monfort recalled to the Associated Press in 2024 that the shoot had been organized by humanitarian aid organization UNICEF in partnership with local Barcelona sports outlet Diario Sport.

Monfort explained to the outlet that the organization had hosted a raffle, inviting those in the Rocafonda neighborhood in the Spanish city of Mataró to enter for a chance to have their picture taken at the iconic FC Barcelona stadium Camp Nou with a player. Yamal’s family just so happened to have won, Monfort said.
Coincidentally, Yamal would go on to debut with FC Barcelona in 2023 and today, he’s heralded as one of the most electrifying stars that the club has ever had.
At Fanatics Fest, Messi, now 39, expressed his admiration for both FC Barcelona and Yamal.
“Lamine is a huge player in which I follow a lot because he plays  for a team that I love and I wish him always the best,” Messi said.

Describing Yamal as “one of the leaders worldwide at 19 years of age,” Messi acknowledged that the World Cup finals could prove to be one of the biggest moments in not only the young player’s life but also in soccer history.
“He has his whole career ahead of him,” Messi said. “He has a great opportunity to attain something historic — which we intend to give our maximum so that it doesn’t happen this time.”

For soccer fans, the photo has become proof of a cosmic connection between the two players. For starters, Yamal and Messi, along with their respective teams, have been competing on opposite sides of the World Cup bracket for the six-week tournament. The only way they would’ve met on the pitch is at the finals — something that will evidently come to pass following Spain’s defeat of France 2-0 in the semifinals on July 14.

Similarities abound between the two players as well. And Yamal has been recognized as somewhat of a successor to the Argentinian soccer icon in Barcelona. Fans and players alike say the rising star has restored some of the dominant energy that Messi once established at the club. Many have joked that through the photoshoot, Messi passed on some of his “sacred” soccer prowess to Yamal.

title: Why Samantha Morton Refused to Do a ‘Deep Dive’ on Circe Before Playing Her in ‘The Odyssey’
summary: Samantha Morton tells TODAY.com about how she prepared to play Circe in “The Odyssey” and her scene that, believe it or not, isn’t CGI.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.
Christopher Nolan’s epic, “The Odyssey,” has finally landed and is already breaking box office records as fans eagerly flock to theaters to see Nolan’s sweeping adaptation of Homer’s classic poem.
Led by an all-star cast including Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland and Robert Pattinson, one actor in particular has been grabbing headlines, and it’s Samantha Morton.

The two-time Oscar nominee, 49, has appeared in a variety of film and TV roles over the years including Steven Spielberg’s “Minority Report” and the AMC juggernaut, “The Walking Dead.” But it’s her turn as Circe, the powerful goddess who seduces Odysseus (Damon) and his battered crew, that’s earning rave reviews, starting with Nolan himself.
“This was a massive film and she is someone who comes in and changes the dynamic,” he told the Los Angeles Times. “In some weird way, the film lived or died over that character. She was the fulcrum.
“After one of Samantha’s takes, the crew gave her a great round of applause ... the last time that had happened was with Heath Ledger on ‘The Dark Knight,’” he added.
Morton credited the entire crew after hearing Nolan’s praise.

“Without giving anything away, there’s a scene that I do that people cannot believe is not CGI, so I think the clap was —obviously, it was lovely, they were clapping (for) Circe — but there was also this sense that ... everything that we did came together,” she said. “And I’ll never forget it.”

After her joint interview with Charlize Theron and Zendaya, Morton stays behind in TODAY.com’s Orange Room in Studio 1A to talk about her notable turn in one of the year’s biggest movies, including why she didn’t spend a lot of time researching her famous character.

title: I’m A Psychologist. Here’s What We Can Learn From ‘Love Island USA’ Winners Bryce and Trinity
summary: Psychologists and family therapists share relationship gems from “Love Island USA” Season 8 winners, Bryce and Trinity, that viewers can implement in their own lives.
story: Take it From Me is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment,  psychologists and family therapists share the relationship gems from “Love Island USA” that viewers can implement in their own lives.

Reality dating shows may not be the first place that come to mind when looking for role models, but experts say that the latest winners of “Love Island USA” are conducting their relationship in ways from which we can all learn.

Season 8 stars Trinity Tatum and Bryce Alakai were crowned the winners of the dating competition show during its July 12 finale. TODAY.com hit up some psychologists to hear about what the professionals think about the pair’s romance that all started in their six-week drama-filled summer in Fiji. And it turns out, we can take a page from the couple’s book on communication, patience and tackling hard conversations, the professionals say.

“For a young couple in this context, I feel like they bring forth a lot of wisdom,” Joanne Broder, media psychologist and fellow at the American Psychological Association, tells TODAY.com. “They’re really honest and just very transparent.”

Since the show wrapped, the couple, who left the villa $100,000 richer in prize money, has been spending time together in Los Angeles. They joined TODAY on July 15 to spill some details about their entry into the real world. So far, they told TODAY’s Craig Melvin, they’re dealing with a touch of separation anxiety.

“Something we weren’t anticipating was just how much our connection has affected us outside of here, too,” Bryce said. “Anytime she’s like, ‘I’m gonna go run this errand,’ I’m like, ‘Where’s she going?’ Like, my heart rate starts. I’m like, ‘What’s going on right now?’”
Trinity also shared that she wants “to be wherever Bryce is.”
“I don’t like being away from him,” she said.

While Trinity, 22, and Bryce, 30, have developed an inseparable bond, their connection didn’t necessarily start out hot and heavy. The two coupled up on their first night on the island, however they both expressed some concerns over their 8-year age gap. And when it came time to decide between locking in with one another or continuing to explore other options, they both chose to take the leap and see if they had chemistry with other incoming contestants.

However, sparks failed to fly with the other bombshells and the pair quickly found themselves back together. At one point, Bryce wanted to see if he felt any potential connection with fellow cast member Kayda, telling Trinity that he hoped to test the waters. But when Kayda didn’t return the sentiment, Bryce and Trinity continued to move forward, gradually getting to know one another and strengthening their physical and emotional bond.
By the end of the season, the two not only cemented their titles as boyfriend and girlfriend, they were also the only couple to say the magic three words “I love you” to each other.
As the winners of “Love Island USA” Season 8 begin to navigate the real world, here’s what people can learn from their journey inside the villa, according to psychologists.
Building a Friendship
One of the most compelling aspects of the pair’s relationship on the island was their pace, psychologists say.
Tracy Meyer, a psychology professor at Collin College in Texas, tells TODAY.com that the couple proves “slow and steady wins the race.”

“While it wasn’t sunshine and rainbows for them at first sight, they were willing to see where the relationship would take them,” Meyer said. “Their relationship mirrors real life more than the others on the show, as they were around temptation regularly, but chose not to let it affect them.”
Meyer adds that as the days went by, the couple continued to choose each other, making a conscious effort to understand the other.
“In the end, even the other contestants on the island recognized that what Bryce and Trinity had was a deeper level of connection that went beyond physical attraction and initial lust,” Meyer says.

Apryl Alexander, a professor at UNC Charlotte’s department of health management and policy, tells TODAY.com that the “slow burn” of the couple’s bond proved to viewers that friendship should remain central to peoples’ romantic relationships.

“When you’re developing a friendship, you are taking the time to get to know one another, be curious, build that connection,” Alexander, who has a background in forensic psychology and child and family therapy. “And for them, their connection expanded to where we got in the finale — where they’re expressing love for each other.”
Tackling the Tough Stuff

The experts also underscored how the healthy communication between Trinity and Bryce stood out, particularly as the pair tackled some difficult conversations. The couple’s age gap was among the stickier topics that they openly discussed on the show. In some of the earlier episodes, Bryce expressed concerns over the age differential, mulling over the issue, even seeking advice from friends.

“There is this weird thing with Trinity and the age gap,” Bryce said, while confiding in fellow islander and bestie Zach Georgiou. “I’m the oldest one here, she’s the youngest. You really fill into who you are from 22 to 26 when you get those experiences. I don’t want to steal her youth.”

The pair also opened up about their concerns to their families during the July 9 episode of the show, with Trinity admitting that the age gap was initially “scary.” But as the couple’s relationship evolved, her fears subsided. And in the recent interview with TODAY, Bryce told Craig that the issue ended up “completely disappearing in my mind.”
Alexander said that the couple’s consciousness and open dialogue around the issue was key to overcoming their concerns.

“Bryce kept bringing up the age gap conversation — that he had some concerns around that, particularly whether or not Trinity, as the person who he perceived as significantly younger, wanted to take the time to explore and date more,” Alexander said. “I love the transparency in that — making sure that he wasn’t being manipulative or exuding any kind of power dynamics because of his age and status.”

There was also the issue of the struggles around interracial dating. During the franchise’s infamous Casa Amor episodes — in which the guys and girls are split up and tested with a slew of new bombshells — Trinity got vulnerable about her insecurity that Bryce could choose to couple up with another woman. It’s a fear, she said, that’s particularly daunting as a woman of color and one that she had previously surfaced to Bryce.

“It’s still really f------ scary, a woman of color talking to someone outside of their race and to see them go back to something that they’re comfortable with,” she told fellow castmate Aniya Harvey through tears. “It’s just one of my biggest fears, which he knows.”

Alexander explained that it’s important for interracial couples to be open about their experience with race and remain upfront with any concerns they may have — especially because ignoring the topic can only have negative effects down the line.

“In other reality shows, when interracial relationships are being introduced or tested, people try to take it with a colorblind approach. That can only last for so long,” Alexander said. “You have to have these tough conversations on what does it mean to be able to navigate an interracial or intercultural relationship? It was a great start for them to be able to start this conversation and model it for viewers.”
Broder added that having difficult conversations can only bring couples closer.
“It’s when you avoid those conversations… that’s when you start experiencing cracks,” she said.
Advice for Their Relationship Outside the Villa
Now that the two are out of the villa, the experts said that they hope the pair can continue to be transparent and avoid allowing their frequent communication from going by the wayside.

“Life is full of challenging moments. They made it off the island and they’re in a good place,” Broder said. “I’m rooting for them. I would tell them to keep doing what they’re doing, and I wish them all the best, and keep having those hard, vulnerable conversations.”

title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders 2026-2027: Who’s New and Who’s Returning?
summary: The 2026-2027 Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad has officially been selected. See a full list of returning veterans and bios for the rookies.
story: They came, they kicked, they conquered: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad have officially announced their 2026-2027 squad.

The latest season of Netflix’s docuseries “America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders,” which premiered in June, captured yet another pressure-packed audition and performance season — showcasing how the team’s growing fame continues to affect its culture.
As interest in the squad continues to soar, the DCC received 55% more applications in 2026 than in 2025, according to the organization.

This year, there are 28 veterans and eight rookie members, including multiple comeback athletes who were cut during auditions in 2025. Read on to meet the rookies, and see the full list of returning members.
Who Are the Rookies on the 2026-2027 Squad?
Amaiyah Naulls

Amaiyah Naulls is an alum of California State University, Fullerton, where she helped lead her Division 1 Pom team to its first ever UDA National Championship at the National Collegiate Dance Team Championship in 2025 as a team captain.
Before making the team, she participated in one of the team’s prep intensives in 2025, per her Instagram.
In an Instagram post announcing her official rookie status, Naulls reflected on her early experience with the DCC and the friends she’s already made along the way.

“This journey has been the most incredible blessing I’ve ever experienced,” she wrote. “And to all the girls I’ve met during this process I love y’all down bad. You are truly my rookie sisters, and our bond goes so far beyond dance. I couldn’t imagine a more perfect group.”
Aubrey Rogers
Aubrey Rogers is a College of the Canyons alum from Santa Clarita, California, and a former Los Angeles Laker Girl.
After two seasons dancing in purple and gold, Rogers is officially adorning a blue-and-white set — and she “can’t wait,” according to her latest post on Instagram.

“This has been the greatest blessing and a dream come true,” Rogers captioned her post announcing her spot on the team. “I can’t wait to wear this iconic uniform and carry on such an incredible legacy. Forever grateful.”
Brianne “Bri” Lindenau
Some fans may recognize rookie Brianne “Bri” Lindenau from when she auditioned for the DCC during the 2025-2026 season.

While Lindenau was disappointed she didn’t receive the outcome she was “hoping and praying for” that time around, per a July 2025 Instagram post, she returned the following year even more determined to earn her spot on the squad.

“Knowing what it feels like to not make this team makes me just extremely grateful and humbled to be back on this field, and it makes this outcome mean that much more,” she wrote in an Instagram post announcing her spot on the 2026-2027 squad. “The comeback is always greater than the setback.”
Lindenau is also an alum of the University of Arizona, where she was a standout member of the Arizona Pomline.
Emily Awbrey
Oregon native Emily Awbrey is another “comeback girl” of the season.

Awbrey previously auditioned for the 2025-2026 season, where team director Kelli Finglass described her personality as “very authentic” on “America’s Sweethearts,” and added that she was “one of the strongest dance technicians in the entire audition” during the first round.
Although Awbrey didn’t leave her first training camp with a uniform, she eventually earned her blue-and-white starred set during the 2026 tryouts.
Afterward, the University of Arizona dance alum posted a compilation of her loved ones’ reactions to her showing that she made the team — custom uniform and all.
“No words can decribe this feeling. All I can think to say for now- Thank you,” she captioned the emotional video, adding a spirited blue heart. “Man i’m blessed.”
Haley Bogdon
For University of Arkansas alum Haley Bogdon, joining the DCC squad won’t require much of a relocation. The rookie is from Frisco, Texas, a suburb just north of Dallas.
“I will never forget this moment! Beyond blessed!!!” Bogdon commented on a photo carousel of her and the other rookies being fitted for their new uniforms on the team’s official Instagram page.
Bogdon is also a former dancer for the University of Arkansas Razorbacks.
Kate Rogge
Kate Rogge, another Texas native from Austin, Texas, also joins the rookie class.
Rogge auditioned in 2025, too, per her Instagram, but didn’t receive a spot on the squad until 2026.
Rogge was also a cheer and pom dancer at her alma mater, University of Texas Austin, where she studied public relations, according to her LinkedIn.
Lexi Smith
Lexi Smith danced on the University of Central Florida spirit team for four years, wrapping up her college career in May and earning a spot on the DCC roster in July.
The rookie from Orlando, Florida wrote on her Instagram that “words cannot describe how much gratitude” she felt throughout tryouts.

“This experience has not only helped me grow as a dancer but also as a person,” she added in the caption of the photo carousel. “I am so beyond thankful for all the people I have met throughout this process, and I can’t believe that I am now a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader!”
Savanna Dastrup
As “America’s Sweethearts” Season 3 viewers saw, Utah native Savanna Dastrup arrived to the team’s 2025 tryouts in pursuit of what she described as a lifelong dream.
But after being cut in the final round, she asked Finglass and DCC head choreographer Judy Trammell if she might have a shot if she returned the following year.
“I do. I mean, you might just chalk this up to timing and experience and the pressure,” Finglass replied. “But, no, I think you’ve got skills to make this team or another team.”
Upon returning for round two in 2026, the Texas Christian University alum officially earned her rookie title.

“Happiest happy tears!! truly a moment i will never forget!! my heart is so full & i am so so grateful !!” she commented on a video the DCC posted on its official Instagram page, adding team-themed emojis.
